p: It is a truth universally acknowledged, that a single man in possession of a good fortune must be in want of a wife.
一个人拥有大量财富，必定需要找一个妻子。

However little known the feelings or views of such a man may be on his first entering a neighbourhood, this truth is so well fixed in the minds of the surrounding families, that he is considered as the rightful property of some one or other of their daughters.
无论一个单身汉在邻居中多么不知名，这个真理在周围家庭中根深蒂固，他被视为某个家庭的女儿的合法财产。
“My dear Mr. Bennet,” said his lady to him one day, “have you heard that Netherfield Park is let at last?”
“亲爱的贝内特先生，”他的夫人有一天对他说，“你听说那纳特菲尔德庄园最后出租了吗？”
Mr. Bennet replied that he had not.
贝内特先生没有回答。
“But it is,” returned she; “for Mrs. Long has just been here, and she told me all about it.”
“但是是的，”她喊道，“因为长妈妈昨天刚来过，她告诉我一切。”
Mr. Bennet made no answer.
贝内特先生没有回答。
“Do not you want to know who has taken it?” cried his wife, impatiently.
“你想要知道是谁租了它？”他妻子急切地问道。
“You want to tell me, and I have no objection to hearing it.”
“你想要告诉我，我没有什么不可以听的。”
This was invitation enough.
这已经足够了。

“Why, my dear, you must know, Mrs. Long says that Netherfield is taken by a young man of large fortune from the north of England; that he came down on Monday in a chaise and four to see the place, and was so much delighted with it that he agreed with Mr. Morris immediately; that he is to take possession before Michaelmas, and some of his servants are to be in the house by the end of next week.”
为什么， dear ，你必须知道，隆太太说纳特菲尔德被一位来自英格兰北部的富翁的年轻人占据；他周一乘四轮马车来看这个地方，就被这里深深吸引，于是立即与莫里斯先生达成协议；他要在九月三十日前入住，而且他的一些仆人会在下周末前住进房子。
“What is his name?”
“他的名字是什么？”
“Bingley.”
“宾利。”
“Is he married or single?”
“他结婚了吗？”
“Oh, single, my dear, to be sure!
“哦，单身，亲爱的，当然！”
A single man of large fortune; four or five thousand a year.
一个拥有大量财富的单身汉；四五千年薪。
What a fine thing for our girls!”
这真是件好事给我们的小姐们！
“How so? how can it affect them?”
“怎么？这怎么能影响她们？”
“My dear Mr. Bennet,” replied his wife, “how can you be so tiresome?
“亲爱的 Bennet 先生，”妻子回答说，“你怎么会这么烦人？”
You must know that I am thinking of his marrying one of them.”
你知道，我正考虑让他娶其中一个。
“Is that his design in settling here?”
“这是他的定居计划吗？”
“Design?
“计划？”
Nonsense, how can you talk so!
噢，胡说八道！你怎么能这么说话！
But it is very likely that he may fall in love with one of them, and therefore you must visit him as soon as he comes.”
但是很可能他会爱上其中一个，因此你必须在他来的时候见他一面。
“I see no occasion for that.
“我看不出有什么必要。
You and the girls may go—or you may send them by themselves, which perhaps will be still better; for as you are as handsome as any of them, Mr. Bingley might like you the best of the party.”
你们和小姐们可以去，或者你们可以派人去，这也许更好；因为你们比她们中的任何一个都漂亮，Bingley 先生可能会喜欢你们中的最好的。
“My dear, you flatter me.
“亲爱的，你夸奖我了。
I certainly have had my share of beauty, but I do not pretend to be anything extraordinary now.
我确实有过一些美丽，但现在我不再自夸了。
When a woman has five grown-up daughters, she ought to give over thinking of her own beauty.”
当一个女人有五个成年的女儿时，她应该停止考虑自己的美丽。
“In such cases, a woman has not often much beauty to think of.”
“在这种情况下，一个女人很少会想到自己的美丽。”
“But, my dear, you must indeed go and see Mr. Bingley when he comes into the neighbourhood.”
“但是，亲爱的，你必须一定要去见见 Bingley 先生，当他进入邻近地区时。”
“It is more than I engage for, I assure you.”
"我答应的远不止这些。"
“But consider your daughters.
"不过想想你的女儿们吧。"
Only think what an establishment it would be for one of them.
只要想想，一个女儿会是什么样的局面。
Sir William and Lady Lucas are determined to go, merely on that account; for in general, you know, they visit no new comers.
莱斯特伯爵和路易丝夫人决定去，仅仅因为这一点；因为你们知道，他们从来不接待新来的客人。
Indeed you must go, for it will be impossible for us to visit him, if you do not.”
确实，你必须去，因为如果我们不带你去，我们无法拜访他。
“You are over scrupulous, surely.
"你太谨慎了，对吧。"

I dare say Mr. Bingley will be very glad to see you; and I will send a few lines by you to assure him of my hearty consent to his marrying whichever he chooses of the girls—though I must throw in a good word for my little Lizzy.”
我敢肯定，伯明翰先生会很高兴见到你的；我会给你寄几封信，保证他同意他娶哪个女儿——尽管我必须给小丽兹加个好话。"
“I desire you will do no such thing.
"我要求你不要这样做。"
Lizzy is not a bit better than the others: and I am sure she is not half so handsome as Jane, nor half so good-humoured as Lydia.
小丽兹并不比其他任何一个好，我敢肯定她并不比简漂亮，也不比莉亚德好脾气。
But you are always giving her the preference.”
但是你总是给她优先。
“They have none of them much to recommend them,” replied he: “they are all silly and ignorant like other girls; but Lizzy has something more of quickness than her sisters.”
"他们没有一个值得推荐的，"他回答说："他们都是愚蠢和无知的，和其他女孩一样；但小丽兹比她的姐妹们快一些。"
“Mr. Bennet, how can you abuse your own children in such a way?
"伯恩斯先生，你怎么能这样虐待自己的孩子？
You take delight in vexing me.
你总是让我生气。
You have no compassion on my poor nerves.”
你没有同情心，我的可怜神经。"
“You mistake me, my dear.
"你误解了我，亲爱的。"
I have a high respect for your nerves.
我对你的神经素质非常尊重。
They are my old friends.
他们是我的老朋友。
I have heard you mention them with consideration these twenty years at least.”
我在这二十多年里，一直对你提到他们时，都给予了考虑。
“Ah, you do not know what I suffer.”
“啊，你不知道我承受着什么痛苦。”
“But I hope you will get over it, and live to see many young men of four thousand a year come into the neighbourhood.”
“但希望你能够克服，等到你看到许多年薪四千的年轻男子进入你所在的地区，你就会明白。”
“It will be no use to us, if twenty such should come, since you will not visit them.”
“如果二十个这样的来，对我们来说就没有用处了，因为你不会去拜访他们。”
“Depend upon it, my dear, that when there are twenty, I will visit them all.”
“我亲爱的，当有二十个的时候，我一定会拜访他们所有的。”
Mr. Bennet was so odd a mixture of quick parts, sarcastic humour, reserve, and caprice, that the experience of three-and-twenty years had been insufficient to make his wife understand his character.
贝内特先生是一个混合了敏捷的头脑、辛辣的幽默、保留和任性，这三十多年的经验不足以使他的妻子理解他的性格。
Her mind was less difficult to develope.
她的头脑并不难开发。
She was a woman of mean understanding, little information, and uncertain temper.
她是一个头脑简单、缺乏信息、情绪不稳定的女人。
When she was discontented, she fancied herself nervous.
当她不开心时，她会认为自己神经紧张。
The business of her life was to get her daughters married: its solace was visiting and news.
她的生活就是嫁女儿，她的乐趣就是拜访和消息。
Mr. Bennet was among the earliest of those who waited on Mr. Bingley.
贝内特先生是最早一批等待拜访比内利先生的人之一。
He had always intended to visit him, though to the last always assuring his wife that he should not go; and till the evening after the visit was paid she had no knowledge of it.
他一直有意去拜访他，但总是向妻子保证不会去；直到拜访结束后，他妻子才得知此事。
It was then disclosed in the following manner.
这是后来的解释。
Observing his second daughter employed in trimming a hat, he suddenly addressed her with,—
他注意到他的第二个女儿正在修剪帽子，突然对她说：
“I hope Mr. Bingley will like it, Lizzy.”
“我希望比内利先生会喜欢它，丽兹。”
“We are not in a way to know what Mr. Bingley likes,” said her mother, resentfully, “since we are not to visit.”
“我们不能确定比内利先生喜欢什么，”母亲不满地说，“因为我们不能去拜访。”
“But you forget, mamma,” said Elizabeth, “that we shall meet him at the assemblies, and that Mrs. Long has promised to introduce him.”
“但你忘记了，妈妈，”丽兹说，“我们会在集会上见到他，而且Mrs. Long答应会介绍他。”
“I do not believe Mrs. Long will do any such thing.
“我不相信Mrs. Long会这样做。
She has two nieces of her own.
她有两个自己的侄女。
She is a selfish, hypocritical woman, and I have no opinion of her.”
她是一个自私、虚伪的女人，我对她没有意见。”
“No more have I,” said Mr. Bennet; “and I am glad to find that you do not depend on her serving you.”
“我也没有，”贝内特先生说，“我很高兴发现你并不依赖她为你服务。”
Mrs. Bennet deigned not to make any reply; but, unable to contain herself, began scolding one of her daughters.
贝内特太太没有回答，但她无法控制自己，开始责骂其中一个女儿。
“Don’t keep coughing so, Kitty, for heaven’s sake!
“不要咳嗽了，Kitty，天啊！
Have a little compassion on my nerves.
你可怜我的神经。
You tear them to pieces.”
你撕破它们。”
“Kitty has no discretion in her coughs,” said her father; “she times them ill.”
“凯蒂咳嗽时总是不注意时机。”
“I do not cough for my own amusement,” replied Kitty, fretfully.
“凯蒂咳嗽并不是为了取乐。”
“When is your next ball to be, Lizzy?”
“莉兹，你的下一次舞会是什么时候？”
“To-morrow fortnight.”
“明天的。”
“Ay, so it is,” cried her mother, “and Mrs. Long does not come back till the day before; so, it will be impossible for her to introduce him, for she will not know him herself.”
“是的，是的。”
“Then, my dear, you may have the advantage of your friend, and introduce Mr. Bingley to her.”
“所以，莉兹，你可以先介绍给你的朋友，然后让先生认识她。”
“Impossible, Mr. Bennet, impossible, when I am not acquainted with him myself; how can you be so teasing?”
“不可能，先生，不可能，我还不认识他，你怎么能取笑呢？”
“I honour your circumspection.
“我尊重你的谨慎。”
A fortnight’s acquaintance is certainly very little.
“两周的了解，当然太少。”
One cannot know what a man really is by the end of a fortnight.
两周的时间，一个人是无法了解一个人的真正性格的。

But if we do not venture, somebody else will; and after all, Mrs. Long and her nieces must stand their chance; and, therefore, as she will think it an act of kindness, if you decline the office, I will take it on myself.”
但是，如果我们不尝试，别人会尝试的；毕竟，长嫂和她的姐妹们必须接受这个事实；所以，如果你们拒绝这个职位，我将承担这个责任。”
The girls stared at their father.
女孩子们瞪大了眼睛看着他们的父亲。
Mrs. Bennet said only, “Nonsense, nonsense!”
贝内特太太只是说：“胡说八道！”
“What can be the meaning of that emphatic exclamation?” cried he.
“你认为这些形式和强调它们的重要性都是胡说八道吗？”
“Do you consider the forms of introduction, and the stress that is laid on them, as nonsense?
“你认为形式和强调它们的重要性都是胡说八道吗？”
I cannot quite agree with you there.
我不能完全同意你的看法。
What say you, Mary?
莫莉，你有什么看法？
For you are a young lady of deep reflection, I know, and read great books, and make extracts.”
你是个深思熟虑的年轻小姐，我知道，而且读了很多书，还摘录过。
Mary wished to say something very sensible, but knew not how.
莫莉想说一些很有道理的话，但不知道怎么说。
“While Mary is adjusting her ideas,” he continued, “let us return to Mr. Bingley.”
“在莫莉调整想法的时候，”他继续说道，“我们再回到伯金莱斯先生。”
“I am sick of Mr. Bingley,” cried his wife.
“我讨厌伯金莱斯先生，”他妻子喊道。
“I am sorry to hear that; but why did you not tell me so before?
“我听说了，但我为什么没有在之前告诉你呢？
If I had known as much this morning, I certainly would not have called on him.
如果我知道今天早上知道这么多，我肯定不会去拜访他的。
It is very unlucky; but as I have actually paid the visit, we cannot escape the acquaintance now.”
真是不幸的事，但我们已经付了拜访的费用，现在我们无法避免这种关系了。”

The astonishment of the ladies was just what he wished—that of Mrs. Bennet perhaps surpassing the rest; though when the first tumult of joy was over, she began to declare that it was what she had expected all the while.
妇女们的惊讶和他一样，也许超过其他人；尽管在最初的喜悦过后，她开始宣称她一直预料到。
“How good it was in you, my dear Mr. Bennet!
“你真是太好了，亲爱的 Bennet先生！”
But I knew I should persuade you at last.
但我知道我最终会说服你的。
I was sure you loved your girls too well to neglect such an acquaintance.
我确信你对你的女儿们太爱了，不会忽视这种关系。
Well, how pleased I am!
好的，我很高兴！
And it is such a good joke, too, that you should have gone this morning, and never said a word about it till now.”
这是一个多么好的笑话，你今天早上去了，但直到现在才说！
“Now, Kitty, you may cough as much as you choose,” said Mr. Bennet; and, as he spoke, he left the room, fatigued with the raptures of his wife.
现在，凯瑟琳，你可以尽情咳嗽了，”本内特先生说，他说话的时候已经离开了房间，因为被他妻子的沉醉所累。
“What an excellent father you have, girls,” said she, when the door was shut.
什么 excellent 父亲你们有， girls ，”她说，门关上之后。
“I do not know how you will ever make him amends for his kindness; or me either, for that matter.
我也不知道你怎么才能让他补偿他的 kindness；或者我，也好说。
At our time of life, it is not so pleasant, I can tell you, to be making new acquaintances every day; but for your sakes we would do anything.
在我们这个年纪，你得知道，每天结交新朋友并不那么愉快；但为了你们，我们会做任何事。
Lydia, my love, though you are the youngest, I dare say Mr. Bingley will dance with you at the next ball.”
莉迪亚，我爱人，虽然你是最小的，我敢说班内尔先生在下个舞会上将会和你跳舞。
“Oh,” said Lydia, stoutly, “I am not afraid; for though I am the youngest, I’m the tallest.”
哦，丽迪亚说，坚定地，“我不怕；虽然我是最小的，但我也是最高的。”
The rest of the evening was spent in conjecturing how soon he would return Mr. Bennet’s visit, and determining when they should ask him to dinner.
傍晚其余的时间都花在猜想他何时会来拜访本内特先生，以及决定何时请他来吃晚饭上。
Not all that Mrs. Bennet, however, with the assistance of her five daughters, could ask on the subject, was sufficient to draw from her husband any satisfactory description of Mr. Bingley.
不过，贝内特太太在丈夫面前，尽管有五个女儿的帮助，仍无法获得满意的描述，而她丈夫却未能提供满意的描述。

They attacked him in various ways, with barefaced questions, ingenious suppositions, and distant surmises; but he eluded the skill of them all; and they were at last obliged to accept the second-hand intelligence of their neighbour, Lady Lucas.
他们用各种方式攻击他，用裸露的问题，巧妙的假设，以及遥远的推测，但都被他巧妙地避开了；最后他们不得不接受邻居劳拉·卢卡斯的二手情报。
Her report was highly favourable.
她的报告非常有利。
Sir William had been delighted with him.
布朗威克先生非常喜欢他。
He was quite young, wonderfully handsome, extremely agreeable, and, to crown the whole, he meant to be at the next assembly with a large party.
他很年轻，非常英俊，非常友好，而且，他打算在下一次集会上带着一大群人来。
Nothing could be more delightful!
真的非常愉快！
To be fond of dancing was a certain step towards falling in love; and very lively hopes of Mr. Bingley’s heart were entertained.
喜欢跳舞是爱上某人的一个确定步骤，而且非常活跃地期待着伯金杰尔先生的心。
“If I can but see one of my daughters happily settled at Netherfield,” said Mrs. Bennet to her husband, “and all the others equally well married, I shall have nothing to wish for.”
“如果我能看到我女儿们幸福地定居在诺顿菲尔德，而且所有其他人都同样幸福地结婚，我将没有什么愿望了。”
In a few days Mr. Bingley returned Mr. Bennet’s visit, and sat about ten minutes with him in his library.
几天后，伯金杰尔先生回访了贝内特先生，并在图书馆里与他坐了大约十分钟。
He had entertained hopes of being admitted to a sight of the young ladies, of whose beauty he had heard much; but he saw only the father.
他曾经期待着能够看到年轻小姐们的美丽，但只看到了父亲。
The ladies were somewhat more fortunate, for they had the advantage of ascertaining, from an upper window, that he wore a blue coat and rode a black horse.
女孩子们更加幸运，因为他们能够从上层窗户得知他穿着蓝色外套，骑着黑色马。
An invitation to dinner was soon afterwards despatched; and already had Mrs. Bennet planned the courses that were to do credit to her housekeeping, when an answer arrived which deferred it all.
一个邀请很快就被寄出；当夫人贝内特已经计划了她家的烹饪，当她收到一封回信时，一切都被推迟了。
Mr. Bingley was obliged to be in town the following day, and consequently unable to accept the honour of their invitation, etc. Mrs. Bennet was quite disconcerted.
伯金杰尔先生必须在第二天到伦敦，因此无法接受他们的邀请，等等。贝内特夫人非常困惑。

She could not imagine what business he could have in town so soon after his arrival in Hertfordshire; and she began to fear that he might always be flying about from one place to another, and never settled at Netherfield as he ought to be.
她无法想象他为什么会在如此短的时间内从赫特福德郡来到伦敦；她开始担心他可能永远在四处奔波，而没有定居诺顿菲尔德。
Lady Lucas quieted her fears a little by starting the idea of his
劳拉·卢卡斯稍微平息了她的担忧，提出了他可能一直在飞来飞去，而没有定居诺顿菲尔德的假设。
being gone to London only to get a large party for the ball; and a report soon followed that Mr. Bingley was to bring twelve ladies and seven gentlemen with him to the assembly.
去伦敦参加舞会，结果发现只带了十二位女士和七位男士来参加聚会。

The girls grieved over such a number of ladies; but were comforted the day before the ball by hearing that, instead of twelve, he had brought only six with him from London, his five sisters and a cousin.
女孩子们为此伤心不已，但第二天舞会前，她们听说Bingley先生只带了六位女士和他从伦敦带来的五个姐姐和一个表亲。
And when the party entered the assembly-room, it consisted of only five altogether: Mr. Bingley, his two sisters, the husband of the eldest, and another young man.
当舞会开始时，房间里只有五个人：Bingley先生、他的两个姐姐、大姐姐的丈夫和另一个年轻人。
Mr. Bingley was good-looking and gentlemanlike: he had a pleasant countenance, and easy, unaffected manners.
Bingley先生长得英俊，举止得体：他有一张和善的面容，自然的举止。
His sisters were fine women, with an air of decided fashion.
他的姐姐们是漂亮的女士，有一种决断的风格。

His brother-in-law, Mr. Hurst, merely looked the gentleman; but his friend Mr. Darcy soon drew the attention of the room by his fine, tall person, handsome features, noble mien, and the report, which was in general circulation within five minutes after his entrance, of his having ten thousand a year.
他的妹夫赫斯特先生只是看上去像个绅士；但他的朋友达西先生很快吸引了房间的注意，因为他身材高大、相貌英俊、举止高雅，而且他进入房间后不到五分钟，关于他每年有一万镑收入的传闻就在一般人群中广泛传播。

The gentlemen pronounced him to be a fine figure of a man, the ladies declared he was much handsomer than Mr. Bingley, and he was looked at with great admiration for about half the evening, till his manners gave a disgust which turned the tide of his popularity; for he was discovered to be proud, to be above his company, and above being pleased; and not all his large estate in Derbyshire could save him from having a most forbidding, disagreeable countenance, and being unworthy to be compared with his friend.
男士们认为他是个英俊的男子，女士们认为他比Bingley先生更漂亮，他被人们在晚上一半的时间里都看得很欣赏，直到他的举止引起了厌恶，这使他的受欢迎度逆转。因为他的骄傲，他高于他的公司，高于被高兴；他的大伯爵郡的大量财产无法挽救他，他有一张最令人畏惧、不讨人喜欢的面孔，不值得与他的朋友相比。

Mr. Bingley had soon made himself acquainted with all the principal people in the room: he was lively and unreserved, danced every dance, was angry that the ball closed so early, and talked of giving one himself at Netherfield.
Bingley先生很快就和房间里所有的重要人物都认识了：他活泼、坦率，跳了所有的舞，对舞会结束得这么早感到生气，并且在晚上谈论自己在诺顿菲尔德举办舞会。
Such amiable qualities must speak for themselves.
这些美好的品质必须自说自话。
What a contrast between him and his friend!
他和他朋友之间的对比是多么的鲜明！

Mr. Darcy danced only once with Mrs. Hurst and once with Miss Bingley, declined being introduced to any other lady, and spent the rest of the evening in walking about the room, speaking occasionally to one of his own party.
达西先生只和赫斯特太太、宾利小姐各跳了一支舞，拒绝了任何其他 ladies 的介绍，其余时间则在房间里踱步，偶尔和自己一方的人交谈。
His character was decided.
他的性格已经决定。
He was the proudest, most disagreeable man in the world, and everybody hoped that he would never come there again.
他是世界上最骄傲、最不讨人喜欢的人，大家都希望他永远不会再来这里。
Amongst the most violent against him was Mrs. Bennet, whose dislike of his general behaviour was sharpened into particular resentment by his having slighted one of her daughters.
最猛烈的反对他的是贝内特夫人，她对他的总体行为的厌恶被他轻视她女儿的举动而加剧了。

Elizabeth Bennet had been obliged, by the scarcity of gentlemen, to sit down for two dances; and during part of that time, Mr. Darcy had been standing near enough for her to overhear a conversation between him and Mr. Bingley, who came from the dance for a few minutes to press his friend to join it.
Elizabeth Bennet被迫因为绅士稀缺而错过了两轮舞会；而在其中一段时间里，德贝奇先生站在她附近，听到了他与彬格莱先生之间的对话，彬格莱先生从舞会出来了一会儿，想邀请他的朋友加入。
“Come, Darcy,” said he, “I must have you dance.
“来，达西先生，”他说，“我必须让你跳舞。
I hate to see you standing about by yourself in this stupid manner.
我讨厌看到你一个人呆在这样的愚蠢姿态里。
You had much better dance.”
你最好跳舞。
“I certainly shall not.
“我当然不会。
You know how I detest it, unless I am particularly acquainted with my partner.
你知道我讨厌它，除非我特别熟悉你的舞伴。
At such an assembly as this, it would be insupportable.
在这样的场合里，它会让人无法忍受。
Your sisters are engaged, and there is not another woman in the room whom it would not be a punishment to me to stand up with.”
你的姐妹们已经订婚了，房间里没有一个女人是我愿意和她站在一起的。
“I would not be so fastidious as you are,” cried Bingley, “for a kingdom!
“我不那么挑剔，”比灵斯先生叫道，“为了整个王国！
Upon my honour, I never met with so many pleasant girls in my life as I have this evening; and there are several of them, you see, uncommonly pretty.”
我发誓，我今天晚上见到的漂亮女孩比我一生见到的还要多；而且有几个，你看到，非常漂亮。
“You are dancing with the only handsome girl in the room,” said Mr. Darcy, looking at the eldest Miss Bennet.
“你正在和房间里唯一的漂亮女孩跳舞，”说斯达克先生，看着艾丽丝小姐。
“Oh, she is the most beautiful creature I ever beheld!
“哦，她是最美丽的，我见过！
But there is one of her sisters sitting down just behind you, who is very pretty, and I dare say very agreeable.
但是你姐姐中有一个正在你后面坐着，非常漂亮，我敢说非常讨人喜欢。
Do let me ask my partner to introduce you.”
让我问你的舞伴来介绍你。

“Which do you mean?” and turning round, he looked for a moment at Elizabeth, till, catching her eye, he withdrew his own, and coldly said, “She is tolerable: but not handsome enough to tempt me; and I am in no humour at present to give consequence to young ladies who are slighted by other men.
“你是指谁？”他转身看着艾丽丝小姐，等她看他的时候，他收回了自己，冷淡地说，“她还算可以，但不够漂亮，让我动心；而且我今天心情不好，不愿意和那些被其他男人看不起的年轻小姐交往。
You had better return to your partner and enjoy her smiles, for you are wasting your time with me.”
你最好回到你的舞伴身边，享受她的笑容，因为你在和我浪费时间。”
Mr. Bingley followed his advice.
宾利先生遵从了他的 advice ，回到他妻子身边，享受她的笑容，因为他和我是浪费时间。
Mr. Darcy walked off; and Elizabeth remained with no very cordial feelings towards him.
达西先生径自走了；爱丽丝特则对他没有很亲切的感情。
She told the story, however, with great spirit among her friends; for she had a lively, playful disposition, which delighted in anything ridiculous.
她卻在朋友中講這個故事時興奮極了；因為她生性活潑、愛玩，喜歡任何滑稽的事物。
The evening altogether passed off pleasantly to the whole family.
傍晚整个儿对全家都过得愉快。
Mrs. Bennet had seen her eldest daughter much admired by the Netherfield party.
Bennet太太看见她最大的女儿被纳特菲尔德派的许多人称赞。
Mr. Bingley had danced with her twice, and she had been distinguished by his sisters.
宾利先生和她共舞两次，她也因受到他姐妹们的青睐而不同凡响。
Jane was as much gratified by this as her mother could be, though in a quieter way.
简·妮 approval by this was as great as that of her mother, though in a more subdued manner.
Elizabeth felt Jane’s pleasure.
伊丽莎白感到简的快乐。

Mary had heard herself mentioned to Miss Bingley as the most accomplished girl in the neighbourhood; and Catherine and Lydia had been fortunate enough to be never without partners, which was all that they had yet learnt to care for at a ball.
玛丽听说自己被比尔廷小姐提到，说她是邻近地区最才情洋溢的姑娘；凯瑟琳和莉迪亚幸运地总能成为舞伴，这对她们来说已经足够了，这是她们在舞会上所学到的全部关心对象。
They returned, therefore, in good spirits to Longbourn, the village where they lived, and of which they were the principal inhabitants.
他们因此精神饱满地回到隆伯orough，那是他们居住的村庄，也是他们主要的居民。
They found Mr. Bennet still up.
他们发现宾格尔先生仍然醒着。
With a book, he was regardless of time; and on the present occasion he had a good deal of curiosity as to the event of an evening which had raised such splendid expectations.
手里拿着一本书，他不顾时间；而在目前这个场合，他对晚上会发生的事情颇有兴趣，那晚曾引起如此高的期待。
He had rather hoped that all his wife’s views on the stranger would be disappointed; but he soon found that he had a very different story to hear.
他其实希望他妻子对那位陌生人的看法都会落空；但很快他就发现他要听的故事大不相同。
“Oh, my dear Mr. Bennet,” as she entered the room, “we have had a most delightful evening, a most excellent ball.
哦，我 dear 邦德先生，她进入房间时，“我们度过了一个最愉快的晚上，一个最优秀的舞会。
I wish you had been there.
我希望你当时在那里。
Jane was so admired, nothing could be like it.
简真是备受赞赏，没有什么能比得上。
Everybody said how well she looked; and Mr. Bingley thought her quite beautiful, and danced with her twice.
人人都说她长得漂亮，伯金尼先生认为她非常漂亮，并且两次和她跳舞。
Only think of that, my dear: he actually danced with her twice; and she was the only creature in the room that he asked a second time.
只想想，亲爱的：他竟然和她跳舞两次；而且她是他第二次要求的唯一一个。
First of all, he asked Miss Lucas.
首先，他要求露西小姐。
I was so vexed to see him stand up with her; but, however, he did not admire her at all; indeed, nobody can, you know; and he seemed quite struck with Jane as she was going down the dance.
我看到他和她一起站起来，感到很生气，但无论如何，他并不欣赏她；你知道，没有人可以欣赏她，而且他似乎对简小姐下舞步时的样子感到很惊讶。
So he inquired who she was, and got introduced, and asked her for the two next.
于是他询问她是谁，然后介绍给她，并要求她跳舞的下一位。
Then, the two third he danced with Miss King, and the two fourth with Maria Lucas, and the two fifth with Jane again, and the two sixth with Lizzy, and the Boulanger——”
然后，他和克林小姐跳舞，和玛丽小姐跳舞，和简小姐跳舞，和莉莉小姐跳舞，和丽莎小姐跳舞，和波尔兰先生跳舞——
“If he had had any compassion for me,” cried her husband impatiently, “he would not have danced half so much!
“如果他对我有同情心，”她丈夫不耐烦地说，“他不会跳得这么少！
For God’s sake, say no more of his partners.
请不要再提他的舞伴了。
O that he had sprained his ancle in the first dance!”
哎，简小姐，我亲爱的，我多么高兴啊！
“Oh, my dear,” continued Mrs. Bennet, “I am quite delighted with him.
“亲爱的，”简太太继续说，“我非常高兴。
He is so excessively handsome! and his sisters are charming women.
他长得非常漂亮！他的姐妹们都是非常美丽的女人。
I never in my life saw anything more elegant than their dresses.
我从没见过比他们的衣服更优雅的了。
I dare say the lace upon Mrs. Hurst’s gown——”
我敢说，赫斯特太太的裙子上的蕾丝——
Here she was interrupted again.
这时她又被打断了。
Mr. Bennet protested against any description of finery.
Bennet先生反对任何对华丽服饰的描述。
She was therefore obliged to seek another branch of the subject, and related, with much bitterness of spirit, and some exaggeration, the shocking rudeness of Mr. Darcy.
她因此不得不寻求另一个话题，并且带着极大的精神痛苦和夸张地描述了达西先生的令人震惊的粗鲁。
“But I can assure you,” she added, “that Lizzy does not lose much by not suiting his fancy; for he is a most disagreeable, horrid man, not at all worth pleasing.
“但我可以向你保证，”她补充道，“丽兹并不因为不迎合他的口味而损失太多，因为他是个最讨厌的、令人讨厌的人，根本不值得让人高兴。
So high and so conceited, that there was no enduring him!
他如此高傲，如此自负，以至于没有人能忍受他！
He walked here, and he walked there, fancying himself so very great!
他在这边走，又在那边走，仿佛自己是如此伟大！
Not handsome enough to dance with!
不够英俊，不能跳舞！
I wish you had been there, my dear, to have given him one of your set-downs.
我希望你当时在场，可以给他的一个教训。
I quite detest the man.”
我完全讨厌这个人。
When Jane and Elizabeth were alone, the former, who had been cautious in her praise of Mr. Bingley before, expressed to her sister how very much she admired him.
当简和伊丽莎白单独在一起时，前者在之前对Bingley的赞美上显得有些谨慎，于是向姐姐表达了自己的钦佩之情。
“He is just what a young man ought to be,” said she, “sensible, good-humoured, lively; and I never saw such happy manners! so much ease, with such perfect good breeding!”
“他就是个年轻人应该有的样子，聪明、好脾气、活泼；我从未见过如此轻松自在的举止，又如此完美地拥有良好的教养！”
“He is also handsome,” replied Elizabeth, “which a young man ought likewise to be if he possibly can.
“他也是英俊的，如果他有可能，他应该也是的。
His character is thereby complete.”
他的性格因此就完美了。”
“I was very much flattered by his asking me to dance a second time.
“我被他的第二次邀请感到很荣幸。
I did not expect such a compliment.”
我没有预料到这样的赞美。”
“Did not you?
“你没有？
I did for you.
我是为你做的。
But that is one great difference between us.
但这就是我们之间的最大不同之处。
Compliments always take you by surprise, and me never.
任何的赞美总是让你感到意外，而我从没有过。
What could be more natural than his asking you again?
他怎么可能不让你感到惊讶呢？
He could not help seeing that you were about five times as pretty as every other woman in the room.
他怎么可能不看到你比房间里的其他女人更漂亮五倍呢？
No thanks to his gallantry for that.
不管他的风度如何，这都是他的过错。
Well, he certainly is very agreeable, and I give you leave to like him.
好吧，他确实很讨人喜欢，我允许你喜欢他。
You have liked many a stupider person.”
你已经喜欢过许多愚蠢的人了。”
“Dear Lizzy!”
“亲爱的丽兹！”
“Oh, you are a great deal too apt, you know, to like people in general.
“哦，你知道，你对一般人的喜好太多，你知道，你从不看到别人的缺点。”
You never see a fault in anybody.
“在你的眼里，全世界的人都是好的和愉快的。”
All the world are good and agreeable in your eyes.
“我一生中从没听到你对人类的任何一个人说过坏话。”
I never heard you speak ill of a human being in my life.”
“我不会匆忙对任何人进行谴责；但我总是说我认为的。”
“I would wish not to be hasty in censuring anyone; but I always speak what I think.”
“我知道你这样做的；这正是令人惊讶的地方。”
“I know you do: and it is that which makes the wonder.
“你的好判断力，你竟然如此真诚地看不到别人的愚蠢和荒谬！”
With your good sense, to be so honestly blind to the follies and nonsense of others!
“坦率的言辞在某种程度上是常见的；到处都能见到。”
Affectation of candour is common enough; one meets with it everywhere.
“但坦率地说话，不炫耀或设计，——去取每个人的品质的好的一面，而不说坏的——这是你独有的。”
But to be candid without ostentation or design,—to take the good of everybody’s character and make it still better, and say nothing of the bad,—belongs to you alone.
“所以，你也喜欢这个男人的姐妹们，对吧？”
And so, you like this man’s sisters, too, do you?
“他们的举止并不相称于他的。”
Their manners are not equal to his.”
“当然不是，一开始；但当你们和他们交谈时，她们是非常讨人喜欢的。”
“Certainly not, at first; but they are very pleasing women when you converse with them.
“简·班内特要和她的哥哥住在一起，照顾他的房子；我猜我们不会发现她是一个非常迷人的邻居。”
Miss Bingley is to live with her brother, and keep his house; and I am much mistaken if we shall not find a very charming neighbour in her.”
“简·班内特是简·奥斯汀的妹妹，她会住在班内特家，照顾他的房子；我猜我们不会发现她是一个非常迷人的邻居。”

Elizabeth listened in silence, but was not convinced: their behaviour at the assembly had not been calculated to please in general; and with more quickness of observation and less pliancy of temper than her sister, and with a judgment, too, unassailed by any attention to herself, she was very little disposed to approve them.
“伊丽莎白沉默地听着，但并不完全相信：他们在集会上的行为并没有被普遍认为是讨人喜欢的；而且，由于她妹妹的观察力更敏锐，脾气更不随和，而且由于她没有受到任何对自己进行注意的评判，她对她们并不很乐意认可她们。”
They were, in fact, very fine ladies; not deficient in good-humour when they were pleased, nor in the power of being agreeable where they chose it; but proud and conceited.
事实上，她们都是非常漂亮的女士，高兴时脸上带着好心情，愿意与人相处时也愿意；但她们骄傲且自负。

They were rather handsome; had been educated in one of the first private seminaries in town; had a fortune of twenty thousand pounds; were in the habit of spending more than they ought, and of associating with people of rank; and were, therefore, in every respect entitled to think well of themselves and meanly of others.
她们身材修长，曾在镇上的一所私立中学受过教育；家产有二十万英镑；喜欢挥霍，与地位高的人交往；因此，她们理应认为自己优秀，而对别人却很瞧不起。
They were of a respectable family in the north of England; a circumstance more deeply impressed on their memories than that their brother’s fortune and their own had been acquired by trade.
他们出身于英格兰北部一个 respectable 家族；这比他们哥哥的财富和他们自己的财富都是通过贸易获得这一点，在他们记忆中留下更深刻的印象。
Mr. Bingley inherited property to the amount of nearly a hundred thousand pounds from his father, who had intended to purchase an estate, but did not live to do it.
Bingley继承了他父亲近百万英镑的财产，父亲原本打算购买一个庄园，但没有活到实现这个计划。

Mr. Bingley intended it likewise, and sometimes made choice of his county; but, as he was now provided with a good house and the liberty of a manor, it was doubtful to many of those who best knew the easiness of his temper, whether he might not spend the remainder of his days at Netherfield, and leave the next generation to purchase.
Bingley也打算这样做，有时他选择他的郡，但如今他有了一个好房子和一个庄园，他是否可以度过余生在诺顿菲尔德，让下一代来购买。

His sisters were very anxious for his having an estate of his own; but though he was now established only as a tenant, Miss Bingley was by no means unwilling to preside at his table; nor was Mrs. Hurst, who had married a man of more fashion than fortune, less disposed to consider his house as her home when it suited her.
她们姐妹都很希望他有自己的地产；但尽管他现在只是一个租户，贝内特小姐并不愿意在他家里主持；而赫斯特太太，嫁给一个比财富多一点的时尚，但少一点的财富，也不愿意把她的家看作她的家。
Mr. Bingley had not been of age two years when he was tempted, by an accidental recommendation, to look at Netherfield House.
Bingley在二岁半时被偶然的推荐诱惑去看诺顿菲尔德庄园。
He did look at it, and into it, for half an hour; was pleased with the situation and the principal rooms, satisfied with what the owner said in its praise, and took it immediately.
他看了半个小时，对位置和主要房间满意，对主人的赞美感到满意，立刻买了。
Between him and Darcy there was a very steady friendship, in spite of a great opposition of character.
他和达西之间有一股非常稳定的好友谊，尽管性格大相径庭。

Bingley was endeared to Darcy by the easiness, openness, and ductility of his temper, though no disposition could offer a greater contrast to his own, and though with his own he never appeared dissatisfied.
Bingley被达西的温和、开放和易接近的性格所吸引，尽管没有一种性格可以与他的性格形成更大的对比，尽管他和自己没有不满意的。
On the strength of Darcy’s regard, Bingley had the firmest reliance, and of his judgment the highest opinion.
由于达西的重视，Bingley有坚定的依赖，对达西的判断有最高的评价。
In understanding, Darcy was the superior.
在理解上，达西是超人的。
Bingley was by no means deficient; but Darcy was clever.
Bingley并不差，但达西聪明。
He was at the same time haughty, reserved, and fastidious; and his manners, though well bred, were not inviting.
他同时傲慢、内向、挑剔；他的举止虽然礼貌，但不吸引人。
In that respect his friend had greatly the advantage.
在这个方面，他的朋友占了上风。
Bingley was sure of being liked wherever he appeared; Darcy was continually giving offence.
傅连生确信自己在任何地方都受欢迎；达西则总是在给人添麻烦。
The manner in which they spoke of the Meryton assembly was sufficiently characteristic.
他们对马里顿聚会的谈论足以显示出他们的特点。

Bingley had never met with pleasanter people or prettier girls in his life; everybody had been most kind and attentive to him; there had been no formality, no stiffness; he had soon felt acquainted with all the room; and as to Miss Bennet, he could not conceive an angel more beautiful.
傅连生一生中从未见过比这些人和这些女孩更令人愉快的了；人人都对他非常友好和关注；没有形式，没有僵硬；他很快就和整个房间熟悉起来；至于简小姐，他无法想象出一个更美丽的天使。

Darcy, on the contrary, had seen a collection of people in whom there was little beauty and no fashion, for none of whom he had felt the smallest interest, and from none received either attention or pleasure.
达西相反，他见过一群没有美丽和时尚的人，对他没有任何兴趣，也没有从任何人那里得到任何关注或快乐。
Miss Bennet he acknowledged to be pretty; but she smiled too much.
简小姐他承认她漂亮；但她笑得太频繁了。
Mrs. Hurst and her sister allowed it to be so; but still they admired her and liked her, and pronounced her to be a sweet girl, and one whom they should not object to know more of.
舒尔特夫人和她的妹妹承认这一点；但仍然赞赏她，喜欢她，认为她是一个甜美女孩，他们不会反对认识更多。
Miss Bennet was therefore established as a sweet girl; and their brother felt authorized by such commendation to think of her as he chose.
简小姐因此被确立为甜美女孩；他们的哥哥觉得有这样的称赞，他可以随意想她是什么样子。
Within a short walk of Longbourn lived a family with whom the Bennets were particularly intimate.
位于长伯恩附近住着一个与贝内特家关系密切的家庭。
Sir William Lucas had been formerly in trade in Meryton, where he had made a tolerable fortune, and risen to the honour of knighthood by an address to the king during his mayoralty.
费尔南多·卢卡斯以前在市场镇梅伦顿经商，赚了一笔钱，并因向国王呈递市长报告而荣升为骑士。
The distinction had, perhaps, been felt too strongly.
也许这种优越感太强了。

It had given him a disgust to his business and to his residence in a small market town; and, quitting them both, he had removed with his family to a house about a mile from Meryton, denominated from that period Lucas Lodge; where he could think with pleasure of his own importance, and, unshackled by business, occupy himself solely in being civil to all the world.
他厌恶他的生意和居住在小市场镇；离开它们后，他和他的家人搬到了距离梅伦顿一英里的卢卡斯别墅，称为卢卡斯别墅；在那里他可以为自己的重要性感到愉快，并不受商业事务的束缚，完全专注于与世交好。
For, though elated by his rank, it did not render him supercilious; on the contrary, he was all attention to everybody.

“I shall be very fit to see Jane—which is all I want.”
我要去见简·妮特尔，这已经够了。
“Is this a hint to me, Lizzy,” said her father, “to send for the horses?”
这是不是对我暗示，莉齐，”她父亲说，“去叫马车来？”
“No, indeed.
不，的确不。
I do not wish to avoid the walk.
我不愿避开散步。
The distance is nothing, when one has a motive; only three miles.
距离并不重要，只要心中有目的；三里而已。
I shall be back by dinner.”
我回来吃饭了。
“I admire the activity of your benevolence,” observed Mary, “but every impulse of feeling should be guided by reason; and, in my opinion, exertion should always be in proportion to what is required.”
“我钦佩你慷慨的行为，”莫莉说道，“但一切情感的冲动都应受理性的指导；在我看来，行动应与所需相适应。”
“We will go as far as Meryton with you,” said Catherine and Lydia.
“我们和你们一起去米尔顿，”凯瑟琳和莉迪亚说道。
Elizabeth accepted their company, and the three young ladies set off together.
莉莉亚和她们一起出发了。
“If we make haste,” said Lydia, as they walked along, “perhaps we may see something of Captain Carter, before he goes.”
“如果我们快点走，或许我们可以在之前见到卡特尔少校。”莉迪亚说道，她们边走边说。

In Meryton they parted: the two youngest repaired to the lodgings of one of the officers’ wives, and Elizabeth continued her walk alone, crossing field after field at a quick pace, jumping over stiles and springing over puddles, with impatient activity, and finding herself at last within view of the house, with weary ancles, dirty stockings, and a face glowing with the warmth of exercise.
在米尔顿她们分手了：两个最年轻的小姐去拜访一位军官的妻子的住所，而伊丽莎白继续她的独行，跨过一片又一片的田野，以快速的步伐跳跃过篱笆和跳过水坑，带着急切的活动，最后在望见房子的视线里，筋疲力尽，脏兮兮的丝袜，脸上因为运动而发烫。
She was shown into the breakfast parlour, where all but Jane were assembled, and where her appearance created a great deal of surprise.
她被带进早餐厅，除了简以外，所有人都在那儿，她的出现引起了极大的惊讶。

That she should have walked three miles so early in the day in such dirty weather, and by herself, was almost incredible to Mrs. Hurst and Miss Bingley; and Elizabeth was convinced that they held her in contempt for it.
霍斯夫妇和比林赛小姐都认为她早上这么早，穿着这么脏的衣服，独自一人行走，几乎是不可思议的；伊丽莎白确信她们认为她轻视她。
She was received, however, very politely by them; and in their brother’s manners there was something better than politeness—there was good-humour and kindness.
她被他们很礼貌地对待，他们兄弟的举止中有一种比礼貌更好的东西——有一种好脾气和善良。
Mr. Darcy said very little, and Mr. Hurst nothing at all.
马克西姆·达西说的很少，霍斯先生什么也没有说。
The former was divided between admiration of the brilliancy which exercise had given to her complexion and doubt as to the occasion’s justifying her coming so far alone.
前者是她对运动给她带来的光彩的赞赏，以及对她独自一人来这么远的原因的怀疑。
The latter was thinking only of his breakfast.
后者只是想着他的早餐。
Her inquiries after her sister were not very favourably answered.
她对姐姐的询问没有得到很满意的答复。
Miss Bennet had slept ill, and though up, was very feverish, and not well enough to leave her room.
费恩伯恩小姐睡得不好，虽然醒着，但很发烧，又不能离开房间。

Elizabeth was glad to be taken to her immediately; and Jane, who had only been withheld by the fear of giving alarm or inconvenience, from expressing in her note how much she longed for such a visit, was delighted at her entrance.
李斯蒂芬高兴地被带去；简则因害怕惊吓或不便，没有在信中表达她多么渴望这样的拜访而感到高兴。她一进门就感到非常高兴。
She was not equal, however, to much conversation; and when Miss Bingley left them together, could attempt little beside expressions of gratitude for the extraordinary kindness she was treated with.
她并不擅长多谈，当贝金莱小姐离开他们两人时，只能表达一些感激之情，因为她对他们所表现出的特别的友好感到非常惊讶。
Elizabeth silently attended her.
李斯蒂芬默默陪伴着她。
When breakfast was over, they were joined by the sisters; and Elizabeth began to like them herself, when she saw how much affection and solicitude they showed for Jane.
早餐结束后，她们被姐妹们接走，李斯蒂芬开始喜欢她们，因为她看到她们对简的关心和照顾。

The apothecary came; and having examined his patient, said, as might be supposed, that she had caught a violent cold, and that they must endeavour to get the better of it; advised her to return to bed, and promised her some draughts.
药房的先生来了，检查了病人，说她得了严重的感冒，必须努力康复；建议她回到床上，还承诺给她一些药水。
The advice was followed readily, for the feverish symptoms increased, and her head ached acutely.
这些建议被很快接受，因为发烧的症状加剧，她的头痛非常厉害。
Elizabeth did not quit her room for a moment, nor were the other ladies often absent; the gentlemen being out, they had in fact nothing to do elsewhere.
李斯蒂芬没有离开她的房间，也没有其他女士经常离开；先生们外出，实际上他们没有其他事情可做。
When the clock struck three, Elizabeth felt that she must go, and very unwillingly said so.
当钟敲到三点时，李斯蒂芬感到必须离开，非常不愿意地说出。

Miss Bingley offered her the carriage, and she only wanted a little pressing to accept it, when Jane testified such concern at parting with her that Miss Bingley was obliged to convert the offer of the chaise into an invitation to remain at Netherfield for the present.
贝金莱小姐提出让她坐车，她只想要一点催促才能接受，当简表示如此担心要离开她时，贝金莱小姐被迫将马车的提议转化为邀请她留在诺顿菲尔德。
Elizabeth most thankfully consented, and a servant was despatched to Longbourn, to acquaint the family with her stay, and bring back a supply of clothes.
李斯蒂芬非常感谢地同意了，一个仆人被派去长布伦镇告诉家人她的停留，并带来一些衣服。
At five o’clock the two ladies retired to dress, and at half-past six Elizabeth was summoned to dinner.
五点整，两位小姐去梳妆，六点半，伊丽莎白被叫去赴宴。
To the civil inquiries which then poured in, and amongst which she had the pleasure of distinguishing the much superior solicitude of Mr. Bingley, she could not make a very favourable answer.
对于这些询问，她不能做出很合适的回答，尤其是对比内斯伍德先生的关心，她感到很荣幸。
Jane was by no means better.
简的情况也不好。

The sisters, on hearing this, repeated three or four times how much they were grieved, how shocking it was to have a bad cold, and how excessively they disliked being ill themselves; and then thought no more of the matter: and their indifference towards Jane, when not immediately before them, restored Elizabeth to the enjoyment of all her original dislike.
妹妹们听到这消息后，重复了几次，表示她们很遗憾，很震惊，因为她们觉得有感冒很糟糕，她们也觉得自己很讨厌生病，然后她们就不再关心这件事了：当她们不在身边时，她们对简的冷漠恢复了伊丽莎白对她的原生厌恶。
Their brother, indeed, was the only one of the party whom she could regard with any complacency.
事实上，她哥哥是她唯一能对她表示满意的人。
His anxiety for Jane was evident, and his attentions to herself most pleasing; and they prevented her feeling herself so much an intruder as she believed she was considered by the others.
他对简的关心很明显，他对自己的关心也很令人愉快，她们阻止了她觉得自己是如此的入侵者，她们对简的冷漠恢复了伊丽莎白对她的原生厌恶。
She had very little notice from any but him.
她几乎没有收到任何人的消息，除了他。

Miss Bingley was engrossed by Mr. Darcy, her sister scarcely less so; and as for Mr. Hurst, by whom Elizabeth sat, he was an indolent man, who lived only to eat, drink, and play at cards, who, when he found her prefer a plain dish to a ragout, had nothing to say to her.
简被马德里先生吸引，妹妹也一样；而对赫斯特先生，伊丽莎白坐的，他是个懒惰的人，只活在吃喝玩乐中，当她发现他更喜欢简单的菜肴而不是烩菜时，他什么也没说。
When dinner was over, she returned directly to Jane, and Miss Bingley began abusing her as soon as she was out of the room.
餐后，她直接回到简身边，简开始责怪她，她刚离开房间就开始。
Her manners were pronounced to be very bad indeed,—a mixture of pride and impertinence: she had no conversation, no style, no taste, no beauty.
她的举止被宣布为非常糟糕，是一个混合了骄傲和不敬的混合体：她没有对话，没有风格，没有品味，没有美丽。
Mrs. Hurst thought the same, and added,—
露西，我夫人认为同样的，还补充道：
“She has nothing, in short, to recommend her, but being an excellent walker.
“她没有什么可以推荐她的，除了是一个优秀的步行者。”
I shall never forget her appearance this morning.
我永远不会忘记她今天早上的样子。
She really looked almost wild.”
她真的看起来几乎疯狂。
“She did indeed, Louisa.
“她确实如此，露西。”
I could hardly keep my countenance.
我简直无法保持镇静。
Very nonsensical to come at all!
真是荒唐到这种程度！
Why must she be scampering about the country, because her sister had a cold?
为什么她必须到处乱跑，因为她姐姐生病了？
Her hair so untidy, so blowzy!”
她的头发如此凌乱，如此蓬松！
“Yes, and her petticoat; I hope you saw her petticoat, six inches deep in mud, I am absolutely certain, and the gown which had been let down to hide it not doing its office.”
“是的，而且她的裙子；我希望你看到了她的裙子，六英寸深在泥里，我绝对确定，而且那件已经让到下面遮住的裙子，没有发挥它的作用。”
“Your picture may be very exact, Louisa,” said Bingley; “but this was all lost upon me.
“你的画像可能非常准确，露西，”说比林斯， “但这一切对我都没有什么影响。
I thought Miss Elizabeth Bennet looked remarkably well when she came into the room this morning.
我认为伊丽莎白·班内特今天早上进来时看起来非常健康。
Her dirty petticoat quite escaped my notice.”
她的脏裙子完全逃过了我的注意。
“You observed it, Mr. Darcy, I am sure,” said Miss Bingley; “and I am inclined to think that you would not wish to see your sister make such an exhibition.”
“你注意到它，先生达西，我肯定，”说比林斯， “并且我倾向于认为你不想看到你的姐姐做出这种展览。
“Certainly not.”
“当然没有。”
“To walk three miles, or four miles, or five miles, or whatever it is, above her ancles in dirt, and alone, quite alone! what could she mean by it?
“要走三英里，或者四英里，或者五英里，或者你愿意走多远，超过你的膝盖在泥里，独自一人，完全独自一人！她是什么意思？
It seems to me to show an abominable sort of conceited independence, a most country-town indifference to decorum.”
这看起来像是非常傲慢的独立，对礼仪的漠不关心。
“It shows an affection for her sister that is very pleasing,” said Bingley.
“这显示了她对姐姐的深情，非常令人愉快。”
“I am afraid, Mr. Darcy,” observed Miss Bingley, in a half whisper, “that this adventure has rather affected your admiration of her fine eyes.”
“我怕，先生达西，”说比林斯，半低语，“这冒险活动可能影响了你对她漂亮眼睛的欣赏。”
“Not at all,” he replied: “they were brightened by the exercise.”
“一点也不，”他回答说：“它们被锻炼得更加明亮。”
A short pause followed this speech, and Mrs. Hurst began again,—
一阵短暂的沉默后，Mrs. Hurst再次开口——
“I have an excessive regard for Jane Bennet,—she is really a very sweet girl,—and I wish with all my heart she were well settled.
“我对简·班内特有极高的评价——她真是一个非常善良的女孩——我希望她能够得到很好的安排。
But with such a father and mother, and such low connections, I am afraid there is no chance of it.”
但是，这样一位父亲和母亲，以及如此低下的门第，我担心她没有机会。”
“I think I have heard you say that their uncle is an attorney in Meryton?”
“我想我听到你提到他们叔叔在米尔顿是律师？”
“Yes; and they have another, who lives somewhere near Cheapside.”
“是的；他们还有一个，住在靠近通货街的地方。”
“That is capital,” added her sister; and they both laughed heartily.
“那太棒了。”姐妹俩一起笑了起来。
“If they had uncles enough to fill all Cheapside,” cried Bingley, “it would not make them one jot less agreeable.”
“如果他们有那么多叔叔来填满通货街，那他们就不会觉得少一点有趣了。”
“But it must very materially lessen their chance of marrying men of any consideration in the world,” replied Darcy.
“但是，这将极大地减少他们嫁给世界上的任何体面男人的机会。”
To this speech Bingley made no answer; but his sisters gave it their hearty assent, and indulged their mirth for some time at the expense of their dear friend’s vulgar relations.
这番话被宾利没有回答，但他的姐妹们表示赞同，并在宾利的笑料中享受了一会儿。
With a renewal of tenderness, however, they repaired to her room on leaving the dining-parlour, and sat with her till summoned to coffee.
他们重新恢复了温柔，然后在离开餐厅后回到她的房间，坐在她身边直到被叫去喝咖啡。

She was still very poorly, and Elizabeth would not quit her at all, till late in the evening, when she had the comfort of seeing her asleep, and when it appeared to her rather right than pleasant that she should go down stairs herself.
她仍然非常虚弱，伊丽莎白不愿意离开她，直到晚上很晚，她看到她睡着了，她觉得这似乎比愉快的离开更合适。

On entering the drawing-room, she found the whole party at loo, and was immediately invited to join them; but suspecting them to be playing high, she declined it, and making her sister the excuse, said she would amuse herself, for the short time she could stay below, with a book.
进入客厅，她发现整个聚会都在进行，被立即邀请加入他们；但怀疑他们正在玩高牌，她拒绝了，用姐姐作为借口说她会用书来打发她下去的短暂时间。
Mr. Hurst looked at her with astonishment.
Hurst先生看着她惊讶。
“Do you prefer reading to cards?” said he; “that is rather singular.”
“你更喜欢阅读而不是玩牌？”他说，“那真是奇怪。”
“Miss Eliza Bennet,” said Miss Bingley, “despises cards.
“伊丽莎白·班内特，”宾利小姐说，“鄙视玩牌。”
She is a great reader, and has no pleasure in anything else.”
她是个伟大的读者，对其他任何事物都没有乐趣。
“I deserve neither such praise nor such censure,” cried Elizabeth; “I am not a great reader, and I have pleasure in many things.”
“我不配得到这样的赞美，也不配受到这样的责备，”丽兹说道，“我不是伟大的读者，我对许多事物都感到乐趣。”
“In nursing your sister I am sure you have pleasure,” said Bingley; “and I hope it will soon be increased by seeing her quite well.”
“在照顾你姐姐的过程中，我确信你会感到乐趣，”宾利说道，“我希望看到她恢复健康后，乐趣会增加。”
Elizabeth thanked him from her heart, and then walked towards a table where a few books were lying.
丽兹从心底感谢他，然后走向一张桌子，桌上放着几本书。
He immediately offered to fetch her others; all that his library afforded.
他立刻提出要为她取其他书，他图书馆里所有的书都提供给她。
“And I wish my collection were larger for your benefit and my own credit; but I am an idle fellow; and though I have not many, I have more than I ever looked into.”
“我父亲为什么留下这么小的书收藏呢？”宾利说道，“我父亲是个懒惰的人，尽管他没有很多书，但他有很多书，他从未仔细看过。”
Elizabeth assured him that she could suit herself perfectly with those in the room.
丽兹保证她可以在房间里找到完美的搭配。
“I am astonished,” said Miss Bingley, “that my father should have left so small a collection of books.
“我惊讶极了，”宾利说道，“我父亲为什么留下这么小的书收藏。”
What a delightful library you have at Pemberley, Mr. Darcy!”
“你有如此美好的图书馆，”德纳第先生说道，“你真是个幸运的人。”
“It ought to be good,” he replied: “it has been the work of many generations.”
“它应该很好，”他说道：“它是由许多世代的人所制作的。”
“And then you have added so much to it yourself—you are always buying books.”
“然后你又添加了这么多，”德纳第先生说道，“你总是买书。”
“I cannot comprehend the neglect of a family library in such days as these.”
“我无法理解一个家庭图书馆在这样的日子里的忽视。”
“Neglect!
“忽视！
I am sure you neglect nothing that can add to the beauties of that noble place.
我确信你忽视了任何可以增加那座宏伟地方美丽的东西。
Charles, when you build your house, I wish it may be half as delightful as Pemberley.”
查尔斯，当你建房子的时候，我希望它能有一半那么愉快像佩伯雷亚。
“I wish it may.”
我希望如此。
“But I would really advise you to make your purchase in that neighbourhood, and take Pemberley for a kind of model.
但我强烈建议你到那个地区购买，而把佩伯里格斯作为模范。
There is not a finer county in England than Derbyshire.”
这个郡没有英格兰更好的地方了。
“With all my heart: I will buy Pemberley itself, if Darcy will sell it.”
我的心：我愿意买佩伯里格斯，只要达西愿意卖。
“I am talking of possibilities, Charles.”
我们在谈论可能性，查尔斯。
“Upon my word, Caroline, I should think it more possible to get Pemberley by purchase than by imitation.”
哦，卡罗琳，我想得到佩伯里格斯的可能性比模仿要大得多。

Elizabeth was so much caught by what passed, as to leave her very little attention for her book; and, soon laying it wholly aside, she drew near the card-table, and stationed herself between Mr. Bingley and his eldest sister, to observe the game.
莉莎被什么发生的事情吸引得几乎没注意她的书，她很快把书完全放下，走到桌前，站在比尼西先生和他的大妹妹之间，观察游戏。
“Is Miss Darcy much grown since the spring?” said Miss Bingley: “will she be as tall as I am?”
莉莎小姐，自从春天以来，小姐长高了吗？你认为她会比我高吗？
“I think she will.
我认为会。
She is now about Miss Elizabeth Bennet’s height, or rather taller.”
她现在大约是像伊丽莎白·班内特一样高，或者甚至更高。
“How I long to see her again!
我多么想再见到她！
I never met with anybody who delighted me so much.
我从未遇到过像她这样让人如此喜欢的人。
Such a countenance, such manners, and so extremely accomplished for her age!
她那张脸，那举止，那非常出众的才能！
Her performance on the pianoforte is exquisite.”
她在钢琴上演奏的技艺是极其出色的。
“It is amazing to me,” said Bingley, “how young ladies can have patience to be so very accomplished as they all are.”
我觉得令人惊讶，查尔斯，年轻小姐们怎么会如此有耐心，如此出众！
“All young ladies accomplished!
所有的年轻小姐都算得上是“有教养”。
My dear Charles, what do you mean?”
我亲爱的查尔斯，你这话是什么意思？
“Yes, all of them, I think.
“是的，我这样想。
They all paint tables, cover screens, and net purses.
他们都会画桌子，盖屏风，包手袋。
I scarcely know any one who cannot do all this; and I am sure I never heard a young lady spoken of for the first time, without being informed that she was very accomplished.”
我几乎不知道谁不能做到这些；而且我肯定我从未听说过一个年轻小姐，没有被告知她是非常有教养的。
“Your list of the common extent of accomplishments,” said Darcy, “has too much truth.
“你的‘有教养’清单，有太多的真实性。
The word is applied to many a woman who deserves it no otherwise than by netting a purse or covering a screen; but I am very far from agreeing with you in your estimation of ladies in general.
这个词是用来形容很多个女人的，她们确实值得这个称号，但我不同意你对一般女人的看法。
I cannot boast of knowing more than half-a-dozen in the whole range of my acquaintance that are really accomplished.”
我无法自豪地知道我认识的整个范围中，真正有教养的六个人。
“Nor I, I am sure,” said Miss Bingley.
我确实如此，”说小姐宾格莱。
“Then,” observed Elizabeth, “you must comprehend a great deal in your idea of an accomplished woman.”
“那么，”伊丽莎白说，“你一定明白一个有教养的女人是什么意思。
“Yes; I do comprehend a great deal in it.”
“是的，我确实明白。
“Oh, certainly,” cried his faithful assistant, “no one can be really esteemed accomplished who does not greatly surpass what is usually met with.
“哦，当然了，”他的忠实助手说，“没有人能真正被称作有教养，除非她远远超过通常遇见的。

A woman must have a thorough knowledge of music, singing, drawing, dancing, and the modern languages, to deserve the word; and, besides all this, she must possess a certain something in her air and manner of walking, the tone of her voice, her address and expressions, or the word will be but half deserved.”

芭布里奇夫人和贝内特小姐在上午拜访了病人，他虽然缓慢地恢复，但仍然在恢复；下午，伊丽莎白加入了他们的聚会，在客厅里。
The loo table, however, did not appear.
卫生间的小桌没有出现。
Mr. Darcy was writing, and Miss Bingley, seated near him, was watching the progress of his letter, and repeatedly calling off his attention by messages to his sister.
霍尔先生和贝内特先生正在打桥牌，而霍尔夫人正在观察他们的游戏。
Mr. Hurst and Mr. Bingley were at piquet, and Mrs. Hurst was observing their game.
芭布里奇先生和贝内特先生正在打桥牌，而霍尔夫人正在观察他们的游戏。
Elizabeth took up some needlework, and was sufficiently amused in attending to what passed between Darcy and his companion.
伊丽莎白拿起一些针线活，正在仔细地观看Darcy和他同伴之间的对话。

The perpetual commendations of the lady either on his hand-writing, or on the evenness of his lines, or on the length of his letter, with the perfect unconcern with which her praises were received, formed a curious dialogue, and was exactly in unison with her opinion of each.
女士们对他的手写、笔迹的笔直、信件的长度以及她收到的赞美都给予了热烈的称赞，这形成了一种奇特的对话，与她对每个的评价完全一致。
“How delighted Miss Darcy will be to receive such a letter!”
“多么高兴，亲爱的Darcy小姐收到这样的信！”
He made no answer.
他没有回答。
“You write uncommonly fast.”
“你写得很快。”
“You are mistaken.
“你错了。”
I write rather slowly.”
我写得比较慢。”
“How many letters you must have occasion to write in the course of a year!
“一年里你必须写多少封信！
Letters of business, too!
商务信件！
How odious I should think them!”
我多么讨厌它们！”
“It is fortunate, then, that they fall to my lot instead of to yours.”
那真是幸运，因为他们落到我头上而不是落到你头上。
“Pray tell your sister that I long to see her.”
请告诉你的妹妹，我多么希望见到她。
“I have already told her so once, by your desire.”
我已经告诉她了，正如你所愿。
“I am afraid you do not like your pen.
恐怕你不喜欢你的笔。
Let me mend it for you.
让我帮你修一修。
I mend pens remarkably well.”
我修笔相当好。
“Thank you—but I always mend my own.”
谢谢——但我总是自己缝补。
“How can you contrive to write so even?”
你怎么能想得这么周到以致于写得这么匀称？
He was silent.
他默不作声。

“Tell your sister I am delighted to hear of her improvement on the harp, and pray let her know that I am quite in raptures with her beautiful little design for a table, and I think it infinitely superior to Miss Grantley’s.”
告诉你姐姐我听到她琴技进步的消息很高兴，祈求她知道我非常喜爱她为桌子设计的美丽小作品，我认为它远远优于格兰特利小姐的作品。
“Will you give me leave to defer your raptures till I write again?
你可允许我把我的喜悦推迟到我再写信时再说？
At present I have not room to do them justice.”
目前我没有地方为他们作公正的评价。
“Oh, it is of no consequence.
哦，这无关紧要。
I shall see her in January.
我将在一月见到她。
But do you always write such charming long letters to her, Mr. Darcy?”
但你总是写这样 charming 的长信给她，达西先生？
“They are generally long; but whether always charming, it is not for me to determine.”
他们通常很长，但我不能确定它们是否总是令人愉快。
“It is a rule with me, that a person who can write a long letter with ease cannot write ill.”
我认为写长信对我来说是件容易事，因此我也认为写不好。
“That will not do for a compliment to Darcy, Caroline,” cried her brother, “because he does not write with ease.
这样对达西先生来说不合适，卡罗琳，因为他的字写得不熟练。
He studies too much for words of four syllables.
他过于注重四音节的字。
Do not you, Darcy?”
你呢，达西先生？
“My style of writing is very different from yours.”
我的写作风格与你完全不同。
“Oh,” cried Miss Bingley, “Charles writes in the most careless way imaginable.
哦，碧金斯小姐，查尔斯写得多么粗心大意啊。
He leaves out half his words, and blots the rest.”
他漏掉一半的字，又把剩下的抹掉。
“My ideas flow so rapidly that I have not time to express them; by which means my letters sometimes convey no ideas at all to my correspondents.”
我的想法流动得太快，以至于没有时间表达，因此我的信有时根本传达不出任何信息给我的收信人。
“Your humility, Mr. Bingley,” said Elizabeth, “must disarm reproof.”
你，碧金斯小姐，必须消除责备。
“Nothing is more deceitful,” said Darcy, “than the appearance of humility.
你太不真诚了，达西先生。
It is often only carelessness of opinion, and sometimes an indirect boast.”
有时只是意见的粗心，有时是间接的炫耀。
“And which of the two do you call my little recent piece of modesty?”
谁会把我的最近一点谦虚称为我的小谦虚？

“The indirect boast; for you are really proud of your defects in writing, because you consider them as proceeding from a rapidity of thought and carelessness of execution, which, if not estimable, you think at least highly interesting.
间接的炫耀，因为你真的为你的写作缺陷感到骄傲，因为你觉得它们是由于思维的快速和执行的粗心，这些虽然不值得称赞，但你认为它们是高度有趣的。
The power of doing anything with quickness is always much prized by the possessor, and often without any attention to the imperfection of the performance.
任何事情做得快，总是受到拥戴的，而且往往不注意作品的缺陷。

When you told Mrs. Bennet this morning, that if you ever resolved on quitting Netherfield you should be gone in five minutes, you meant it to be a sort of panegyric, of compliment to yourself; and yet what is there so very laudable in a precipitance which must leave very necessary business undone, and can be of no real advantage to yourself or anyone else?”
当你今天早上告诉贝内特太太，如果你决定离开诺顿菲尔特，你将在五分钟内离开时，你本意是想写一篇赞歌，赞美自己，而不是夸奖自己。然而，有什么值得称赞的匆忙行为，它必须留下重要的事务未做，对自己或任何人也没有实际的好处呢？
“Nay,” cried Bingley, “this is too much, to remember at night all the foolish things that were said in the morning.
“不，”比林斯先生喊道，“这太多了，晚上回想早上说的那些愚蠢的事情。
And yet, upon my honour, I believed what I said of myself to be true, and I believe it at this moment.
但是，我发誓，我确信我所说的是真实的，并且我现在也相信它。
At least, therefore, I did not assume the character of needless precipitance merely to show off before the ladies.”
至少，因此，我并不只是为了在女士们面前炫耀而假设无谓的匆忙。
“I daresay you believed it; but I am by no means convinced that you would be gone with such celerity.
“我敢说你相信了，但是我不认为你一定会如此迅速地离开。

Your conduct would be quite as dependent on chance as that of any man I know; and if, as you were mounting your horse, a friend were to say, ‘Bingley, you had better stay till next week,’ you would probably do it—you would probably not go—and, at another word, might stay a month.”
你的行为会完全取决于偶然，就像我认识的人一样，如果你在骑马时朋友说，‘比林斯先生，你最好等到下星期回来，’你可能会去，你可能会不去，甚至在另一个词的情况下，你可能会待一个月。
“You have only proved by this,” cried Elizabeth, “that Mr. Bingley did not do justice to his own disposition.
“你只是通过这个证明，证明了比林斯先生没有公正地对待他的性格。
You have shown him off now much more than he did himself.”
你表现得比他自己表现得更多。
“I am exceedingly gratified,” said Bingley, “by your converting what my friend says into a compliment on the sweetness of my temper.
“我非常高兴，”比林斯先生说，“通过你的朋友的话，你把我说的话变成了对我的性格的赞美。

But I am afraid you are giving it a turn which that gentleman did by no means intend; for he would certainly think the better of me if, under such a circumstance, I were to give a flat denial, and ride off as fast as I could.”
但是，我担心你正在给它一个方向，那个先生并没有打算；因为如果在这种情况下，我以任何方式否认，我将很快骑马离开。
“Would Mr. Darcy then consider the rashness of your original intention as atoned for by your obstinacy in adhering to it?”
“如果达西先生会认为你的最初意图的无谓性被你的坚持所弥补吗？”
“Upon my word, I cannot exactly explain the matter—Darcy must speak for himself.”
“真的，我不能确切地解释这件事——达西先生必须自己解释。
“You expect me to account for opinions which you choose to call mine, but which I have never acknowledged.
“你期望我解释你认为是我的意见，但是我没有承认。

Allowing the case, however, to stand according to your representation, you must remember, Miss Bennet, that the friend who is supposed to desire his return to the house, and the delay of his plan, has merely desired it, asked it without offering one argument in favour of its propriety.”
尽管如此，如果按照你的描述，你必须记住，宾斯太太，那个被认为希望他回到房子，计划延迟的朋友，只是希望它，没有提供任何理由来支持它的适当性。
“To yield readily—easily—to the persuasion of a friend is no merit with you.”
“轻易地接受朋友的说服是你的美德。”
“To yield without conviction is no compliment to the understanding of either.”
轻易地屈服于朋友的劝说对你来说不是理解力的荣誉。
“You appear to me, Mr. Darcy, to allow nothing for the influence of friendship and affection.
“你看起来似乎对我，斯克里布先生，认为没有什么友谊和感情的影响。”
A regard for the requester would often make one readily yield to a request, without waiting for arguments to reason one into it.
对于请求者的好感往往会让人轻易地屈服，而不必等待理由来说服自己。
I am not particularly speaking of such a case as you have supposed about Mr. Bingley.
我并不是在讨论像您所设想的那样关于斯克里布先生的情况。
We may as well wait, perhaps, till the circumstance occurs, before we discuss the discretion of his behaviour thereupon.
我们也许可以等到情况发生，再讨论他的行为的妥当性。

But in general and ordinary cases, between friend and friend, where one of them is desired by the other to change a resolution of no very great moment, should you think ill of that person for complying with the desire, without waiting to be argued into it?”
但在一般和普通的场合，朋友之间，当一个人被要求改变一个不很重要的决定时，如果你认为这个人对这种人的行为不满意，而不等他被说服，你认为合适吗？

“Will it not be advisable, before we proceed on this subject, to arrange with rather more precision the degree of importance which is to appertain to this request, as well as the degree of intimacy subsisting between the parties?”
“在我们讨论这个问题之前，是否应该更精确地安排一下这个请求的重要性，以及双方之间的亲密程度？”

“By all means,” cried Bingley; “let us hear all the particulars, not forgetting their comparative height and size, for that will have more weight in the argument, Miss Bennet, than you may be aware of.
“当然，”宾利叫道，“让我们听听所有的细节，不要忘记他们的相对高度和大小，因为这在论点中将更有分量，简夫人，你可能不知道。
I assure you that if Darcy were not such a great tall fellow, in comparison with myself, I should not pay him half so much deference.
我保证，如果达西不是那么高大，与我相比，我不会对他那么尊敬。
I declare I do not know a more awful object than Darcy on particular occasions, and in particular places; at his own house especially, and of a Sunday evening, when he has nothing to do.”
我保证我也不知道一个比达西在特定场合和特定地点更可怕的东西是什么，特别是他自己的房子，特别是星期天晚上，当他没有事情可做。
Mr. Darcy smiled; but Elizabeth thought she could perceive that he was rather offended, and therefore checked her laugh.
达西微笑了，但伊丽莎白认为她可以感觉到他似乎有点生气，因此停止了笑。
Miss Bingley warmly resented the indignity he had received, in an expostulation with her brother for talking such nonsense.
宾利夫人强烈地谴责了他所受到的侮辱，对她的哥哥的胡言乱语进行了申辩。
“I see your design, Bingley,” said his friend.
“我看出你的意图，宾利先生。”他的朋友说。
“You dislike an argument, and want to silence this.”
“你不喜欢辩论，想要沉默这个。”
“Perhaps I do.
“也许我也是。”
Arguments are too much like disputes.
争论太像争吵了。
If you and Miss Bennet will defer yours till I am out of the room, I shall be very thankful; and then you may say whatever you like of me.”
如果你们和简·班内特小姐愿意等我出去，我将非常感谢；然后你们可以说我想什么就说什么。
“What you ask,” said Elizabeth, “is no sacrifice on my side; and Mr. Darcy had much better finish his letter.”
“你所要求的，”伊丽莎白说，“对我而言并非牺牲；达西先生最好把信写完。”
Mr. Darcy took her advice, and did finish his letter.
达西先生听从了她的建议，确实写完了信。
When that business was over, he applied to Miss Bingley and Elizabeth for the indulgence of some music.
当这件事结束之后，他向简·班内特小姐和伊丽莎白要求一些音乐的许可。
Miss Bingley moved with alacrity to the pianoforte, and after a polite request that Elizabeth would lead the way, which the other as politely and more earnestly negatived, she seated herself.
班内特小姐敏捷地走到钢琴前，礼貌地请求伊丽莎白领路，伊丽莎白礼貌而坚决地拒绝了，她坐了下来。

Mrs. Hurst sang with her sister; and while they were thus employed, Elizabeth could not help observing, as she turned over some music-books that lay on the instrument, how frequently Mr. Darcy’s eyes were fixed on her.
豪斯利夫人和姐姐一起唱了歌，当她们在演奏时，伊丽莎白忍不住注意到，她翻看一些音乐书时，达西先生的眼睛总是盯着她。
She hardly knew how to suppose that she could be an object of admiration to so great a man, and yet that he should look at her because he disliked her was still more strange.
她几乎不知道怎么想象，她可以成为一个如此伟大男子的欣赏对象，而且，她却因为不喜欢她而看她，这仍然更奇怪。

She could only imagine, however, at last, that she drew his notice because there was something about her more wrong and reprehensible, according to his ideas of right, than in any other person present.
她只能想象，最后，她想象她引他的注意是因为她身上有些东西比在场的其他任何一个人更不正确和可耻，根据他的关于正确的想法。
The supposition did not pain her.
这个假设并不使她痛苦。
She liked him too little to care for his approbation.
她喜欢他，也不在乎他的认可。
After playing some Italian songs, Miss Bingley varied the charm by a lively Scotch air; and soon afterwards Mr. Darcy, drawing near Elizabeth, said to her,—
在演奏了一些意大利歌曲之后，班内特小姐以一种活泼的苏格兰调子变化了魅力，不久之后，达西先生走近伊丽莎白，说：“你简·班内特小姐，是否感到一种强烈的倾向，去抓住这样一个机会跳舞一曲华尔兹？”
“Do you not feel a great inclination, Miss Bennet, to seize such an opportunity of dancing a reel?”
她微笑，但没有回答。
She smiled, but made no answer.
他重复了这个问题，对她的沉默感到惊讶。
He repeated the question, with some surprise at her silence.
他重复了这个问题，有些惊讶于她的沉默。
“Oh,” said she, “I heard you before; but I could not immediately determine what to say in reply.
哦，”她说道，“我之前听到过你，但一时难以确定该说什么来作答。

You wanted me, I know, to say ‘Yes,’ that you might have the pleasure of despising my taste; but I always delight in overthrowing those kind of schemes, and cheating a person of their premeditated contempt.
你想要我，我知道，要说我‘是’，这样你就可以享受到瞧不起我品味的快乐；但我总是喜欢颠覆那些种方案，欺骗一个人预先打算的轻蔑。
I have, therefore, made up my mind to tell you that I do not want to dance a reel at all; and now despise me if you dare.”
因此，我已经决定告诉你，我根本不想跳舞；现在鄙视你，如果你敢。
“Indeed I do not dare.”
“事实上我不敢。”

Elizabeth, having rather expected to affront him, was amazed at his gallantry; but there was a mixture of sweetness and archness in her manner which made it difficult for her to affront anybody, and Darcy had never been so bewitched by any woman as he was by her.
莉莉丝，因为预料到要冒犯他，感到惊讶，但她的举止中有一种甜蜜和狡黠的混合，使得她很难冒犯任何人，而达西从未像对她那样被任何女人迷住过。
He really believed that, were it not for the inferiority of her connections, he should be in some danger.
他真的相信，如果不是因为她的背景不如人家，他可能会遇到危险。
Miss Bingley saw, or suspected, enough to be jealous; and her great anxiety for the recovery of her dear friend Jane received some assistance from her desire of getting rid of Elizabeth.
贝金特小姐看到或怀疑到足够去嫉妒；她对好友简的恢复的极大焦虑，得到了她想摆脱莉莉丝的欲望的某些帮助。
She often tried to provoke Darcy into disliking her guest, by talking of their supposed marriage, and planning his happiness in such an alliance.
她经常试图激发达西不喜欢她的客人，通过谈论他们所设想的婚姻，以及计划他的幸福，通过这种联盟。

“I hope,” said she, as they were walking together in the shrubbery the next day, “you will give your mother-in-law a few hints, when this desirable event takes place, as to the advantage of holding her tongue; and if you can compass it, to cure the younger girls of running after the officers.
“我希望，”她说，第二天和他们一起在灌木丛中散步时说道，“你给你的母亲大人一个提示，当这个令人期待的事件发生时，关于保持沉默的建议；如果可以的话，要治愈年轻女孩们追逐军官的冲动。
And, if I may mention so delicate a subject, endeavour to check that little something, bordering on conceit and impertinence, which your lady possesses.”
如果我提到如此敏感的问题，努力阻止你夫人那点轻浮和冒犯，你太太那点自以为是和冒犯，你夫人那点轻浮和冒犯。
“Have you anything else to propose for my domestic felicity?”
“你有什么别的提议来增加我的家庭幸福？”
“Oh yes.
“哦，是的。
Do let the portraits of your uncle and aunt Philips be placed in the gallery at Pemberley.
让比尔明德小姐和菲利普伯爵的画像放在佩姆伯里尔的画廊里。
Put them next to your great-uncle the judge.
放在比尔明德小姐和法官的旁边。
They are in the same profession, you know, only in different lines.
他们都是同一个行当，只是在不同的领域。
As for your Elizabeth’s picture, you must not attempt to have it taken, for what painter could do justice to those beautiful eyes?”
对于你那伊丽莎白的照片，你可千万不要试图去照相，因为画家们能拍出那些美丽眼睛的美来吗？
“It would not be easy, indeed, to catch their expression; but their colour and shape, and the eyelashes, so remarkably fine, might be copied.”
“这很难捕捉他们的表情，但他们的颜色和形状，以及睫毛，那真是非常精细，或许可以复制。”
At that moment they were met from another walk by Mrs. Hurst and Elizabeth herself.
在那一刻，他们被从另一条走道上遇到的玛丝洛娃和伊丽莎白本人。
“I did not know that you intended to walk,” said Miss Bingley, in some confusion, lest they had been overheard.
“我不知道你们打算走，”贝金德尔小姐有些困惑地说，怕她们被听见了。
“You used us abominably ill,” answered Mrs. Hurst, “running away without telling us that you were coming out.”
“你们对我们非常不友好，”玛丝洛娃回答，“没有告诉我们你们要出来。”
Then taking the disengaged arm of Mr. Darcy, she left Elizabeth to walk by herself.
然后接过Mr. Darcy未抓住的胳膊，她独自一人离开了伊丽莎白。
The path just admitted three.
这条路只容得三个人。
Mr. Darcy felt their rudeness, and immediately said,—
Mr. Darcy感到他们的粗鲁，立刻说——
“This walk is not wide enough for our party.
“这条路不够宽，我们的队伍不够大。”
We had better go into the avenue.”
我们最好进到大道上去。”
But Elizabeth, who had not the least inclination to remain with them, laughingly answered,—
但伊丽莎白，对留在他们身边没有任何兴趣，笑着回答——
“No, no; stay where you are.
“不，不；留下来吧。
You are charmingly grouped, and appear to uncommon advantage.
你们很美地排列着，看起来非常出色。
The picturesque would be spoilt by admitting a fourth.
风景会因此被破坏，如果再进来一个。”
Good-bye.”
再见。”
She then ran gaily off, rejoicing, as she rambled about, in the hope of being at home again in a day or two.
她便兴高采烈地跑走了，高兴地在那儿漫无目的地闲逛，希望在两天内能够回到家中。
Jane was already so much recovered as to intend leaving her room for a couple of hours that evening.
简已经恢复得差不多了，晚上打算出去活动一下。

When the ladies removed after dinner Elizabeth ran up to her sister, and seeing her well guarded from cold, attended her into the drawing-room, where she was welcomed by her two friends with many professions of pleasure; and Elizabeth had never seen them so agreeable as they were during the hour which passed before the gentlemen appeared.
当晚饭后，丽贝卡跑上去到姐姐身边，看到姐姐被严寒所包围，她便陪同姐姐进入画室，那里迎接她们的有两位朋友，她们非常愉快。丽贝卡从未见过她们如此愉快的。

他们的谈话能力很强。

“They arise chiefly from what is passing at the time; and though I sometimes amuse myself with suggesting and arranging such little elegant compliments as may be adapted to ordinary occasions, I always wish to give them as unstudied an air as possible.”
“它们主要来自当时发生的事情；虽然我有时会用一些小的优雅的恭维来适应普通的场合，但我总是希望尽可能给它们一个不经过研究的空气。”
Mr. Bennet’s expectations were fully answered.
贝内特先生的期望得到了完全的满足。

His cousin was as absurd as he had hoped; and he listened to him with the keenest enjoyment, maintaining at the same time the most resolute composure of countenance, and, except in an occasional glance at Elizabeth, requiring no partner in his pleasure.
他的堂兄很荒唐，他一边听一边享受，同时保持了最坚定的面容，除了偶尔看一眼伊丽莎白，他不需要伙伴来分享他的快乐。
By tea-time, however, the dose had been enough, and Mr. Bennet was glad to take his guest into the drawing-room again, and when tea was over, glad to invite him
到茶点时间了，但是剂量已经足够，所以贝内特先生很高兴再次把客人带进客厅，茶点结束后，他很高兴邀请他朗读给女士们听。
to read aloud to the ladies.
贝内特先生的堂兄很快同意了，一本书被拿出来；但当他看到（因为所有宣布都是从循环图书馆借来的）他往后退了一步，请求道歉，抗议说他从不读小说。

Mr. Collins readily assented, and a book was produced; but on beholding it (for everything announced it to be from a circulating library) he started back, and, begging pardon, protested that he never read novels.
贝内特先生的堂兄很快同意了，一本书被拿出来；但当他看到（因为所有宣布都是从循环图书馆借来的）他往后退了一步，请求道歉，抗议说他从不读小说。
Kitty stared at him, and Lydia exclaimed.
贝内特小姐瞪了他一眼，丽迪雅惊呼。
Other books were produced, and after some deliberation he chose “Fordyce’s Sermons.”
其他书籍被拿出来，经过一些考虑，他选择了“福特希奇的讲道”。
Lydia gaped as he opened the volume; and before he had, with very monotonous solemnity, read three pages, she interrupted him with,—
丽迪雅打开书页，她打断了他，以非常单调的庄严的语气读了三页，她打断了他，以非常单调的庄严的语气读了三页。
“Do you know, mamma, that my uncle Philips talks of turning away Richard? and if he does, Colonel Forster will hire him.
“你知道，妈妈，我叔叔菲利普说要将Richard辞退？如果他这样做，科伦·福斯特会雇用他。
My aunt told me so herself on Saturday.
我的姨妈告诉我，她自己在星期六说的。
I shall walk to Meryton to-morrow to hear more about it, and to ask when Mr. Denny comes back from town.”
我明天要步行到米尔顿去听更多的消息，还要问一下，当Mr. Denny回来的时候，他什么时候回来。
Lydia was bid by her two eldest sisters to hold her tongue; but Mr. Collins, much offended, laid aside his book, and said,—
丽迪雅被她两个大姐姐叫住，要保持沉默；但贝内特先生的堂兄，非常生气，放下他的书，说——
“I have often observed how little young ladies are interested by books of a serious stamp, though written solely for their benefit.
“我常常观察到，年轻小姐对严肃的书并不感兴趣，即使它们是专门为她们的益处写的。
It amazes me, I confess; for certainly there can be nothing so advantageous to them as instruction.
我承认，我感到很惊讶；因为他们肯定没有什么比教育更有利于他们了。
But I will no longer importune my young cousin.”
但我不会再再三劝说我的小表妹了。
Then, turning to Mr. Bennet, he offered himself as his antagonist at backgammon.
然后，他转向贝内特先生，提议自己成为他的对手进行象棋。
Mr. Bennet accepted the challenge, observing that he acted very wisely in leaving the girls to their own trifling amusements.
贝内特先生接受了挑战，观察到他明智地把女孩子独自玩的小把戏留给了他们。

Mrs. Bennet and her daughters apologized most civilly for Lydia’s interruption, and promised that it should not occur again, if he would resume his book; but Mr. Collins, after assuring them that he bore his young cousin no ill-will, and should never resent her behaviour as any affront, seated himself at another table with Mr. Bennet, and prepared for backgammon.
贝内特太太和她的女儿们礼貌地道歉了，承诺如果他继续看书，就不会再发生这样的事了；但是柯林斯先生保证他们不会对他小表妹的行为怀有恶意，并且永远不会把她的行为看作是一种冒犯，于是他和贝内特先生一起坐在另一张桌子旁，准备进行象棋。

Mr. Collins was not a sensible man, and the deficiency of nature had been but little assisted by education or society; the greatest part of his life having been spent under the guidance of an illiterate and miserly father; and though he belonged to one of the universities, he had merely kept the necessary terms without forming at it any useful acquaintance.
布朗沃德先生不是一个明智的人，教育和社交对他帮助不大；他大部分时间都在一个没有受过教育且吝啬的父亲的指导下度过；虽然他属于一所大学，但他只是勉强完成了必要的课程，没有形成任何有用的社交关系。

The subjection in which his father had brought him up had given him originally great humility of manner; but it was now a good deal counteracted by the self-conceit of a weak head, living in retirement, and the consequential feelings of early and unexpected prosperity.
他父亲给他带来的屈辱使他最初具有了很好的态度；但现在，由于一个头脑虚弱的人，住在隐居之中，以及早期和意外的繁荣，这些都使他受到了很大的反作用。

A fortunate chance had recommended him to Lady Catherine de Bourgh when the living of Hunsford was vacant; and the respect which he felt for her high rank, and his veneration for her as his patroness, mingling with a very good opinion of himself, of his authority as a clergyman, and his right as a rector, made him altogether a mixture of pride and obsequiousness, self-importance and humility.
一个幸运的机会使他遇到了德伯格伯爵夫人，当时霍恩斯福德的职位空缺；他对她的高贵地位感到尊敬，对她是他的庇护者感到敬畏，将自己与牧师的权威和作为牧师的特权以及作为领主的权利结合在一起，使他成为一个混合了骄傲和顺从、自尊和谦虚的人。

Having now a good house and a very sufficient income, he intended to marry; and in seeking a reconciliation with the Longbourn family he had a wife in view, as he meant to choose one of the daughters, if he found them as handsome and amiable as they were represented by common report.
他现在有一个好房子和一个相当充足的收入，他打算结婚；他寻求与长布伦斯顿家族和解，他有一个妻子在心中，因为他打算选择一个女儿，如果他发现她们像他们被普遍报道的那样漂亮和友善。

This was his plan of amends—of atonement—for inheriting their father’s estate; and he thought it an excellent one, full of eligibility and suitableness, and excessively generous and disinterested on his own part.
这是他的计划，以偿还继承他们父亲的遗产；他认为这是一个很好的计划，符合所有人的利益和适宜，而且非常慷慨和无私，从他的角度来看。
His plan did not vary on seeing them.
他没有看到他们。
Miss Bennet’s lovely face confirmed his views, and established all his strictest notions of what was due to seniority; and for the first evening she was his settled choice.
贝恩斯小姐美丽的脸验证了他的看法，并确立了他对于年长者的严格观念；在第一次早晨，她是他决定的唯一选择。

The next morning, however, made an alteration; for in a quarter of an hour’s tête-à-tête with Mrs. Bennet before breakfast, a conversation beginning with his parsonage-house, and leading naturally to the avowal of his hopes, that a mistress for it might be found at Longbourn, produced from her, amid very complaisant smiles and general encouragement, a caution against the very Jane he had fixed on.
但是第二天早上，发生了变化；因为半小时内，与贝恩斯小姐的交谈，开始于他的牧师住宅，自然地转向了对长布伦斯顿住宅的求婚，她从她，伴随着非常愉快的微笑和普遍的鼓励，警告他，他固定在他选定的那位。

“As to her younger daughters, she could not take upon her to say—she could not positively answer—but she did not know of any prepossession;—her eldest daughter she must just mention—she felt it incumbent on her to hint, was likely to be very soon engaged.”
“至于她的两个女儿，她不能说——她不能完全回答——但她不知道有任何偏见；——她的大女儿她必须提到——她必须提到，她认为很快就会被一个小姐找到。”
Mr. Collins had only to change from Jane to Elizabeth—and it was soon done—done while Mrs. Bennet was stirring the fire.
布朗沃德先生只需从简爱到伊丽莎白，这很快就完成了——在贝恩斯小姐在早餐前搅火时，她完成了。
Elizabeth, equally next to Jane in birth and beauty, succeeded her of course.
伊丽莎白，与简一样出生和美丽，自然地接替了简。
Mrs. Bennet treasured up the hint, and trusted that she might soon have two daughters married; and the man whom she could not bear to speak of the day before, was now high in her good graces.
贝恩斯小姐把这个暗示保存起来，相信她很快会有两个女儿结婚；她不能忍受前一天提到的人现在对她的好感很高。

Lydia’s intention of walking to Meryton was not forgotten: every sister except Mary agreed to go with her; and Mr. Collins was to attend them, at the request of Mr. Bennet, who was most anxious to get rid of him, and have his library to himself; for thither Mr. Collins had followed him after breakfast, and there he would continue, nominally engaged with one of the largest folios in the collection, but really talking to Mr. Bennet, with little cessation, of his house and garden at Hunsford.
辛西娅的打算去米尔顿散步没有被遗忘：除了玛丽以外，每个姐妹都同意去；而布朗沃德先生被要求陪同他们，因为贝恩斯先生最担心让他离开，让他独自享受他的图书馆；因为布朗沃德先生在早餐后跟随他，他将在那里继续，名义上与一本最大的卷轴交谈，但实际上与贝恩斯先生交谈，几乎没有停止，谈论霍恩斯福德的房屋和花园。
Such doings discomposed Mr. Bennet exceedingly.
这些事情使贝恩斯先生非常烦恼。

In his library he had been always sure of leisure and tranquillity; and though prepared, as he told Elizabeth, to meet with folly and conceit in every other room in the house, he was used to be free from them there: his civility, therefore, was most prompt in inviting Mr. Collins to join his daughters in their walk; and Mr. Collins, being in fact much better fitted for a walker than a reader, was extremely well pleased to close his large book, and go.
在他的图书馆里，他总是有闲暇和宁静；尽管他告诉伊丽莎白，他准备在房子的其他房间中遇到愚蠢和自负，但他习惯于在那里不受这些影响；他的礼貌，因此，非常迅速地邀请布朗沃德先生加入他的女儿们散步；而布朗沃德先生，事实上比读者更适合散步，非常高兴地关闭了他的大书，去散步。
In pompous nothings on his side, and civil assents on that of his cousins, their time passed till they entered Meryton.
在他们这边是洋洋得意的废话，在他们那边是礼貌的同意，时间就这样过去了，直到他们进入了梅伦顿。
The attention of the younger ones was then no longer to be gained by him.
年轻人的注意力此时已经不再吸引他们了。
Their eyes were immediately wandering up the street in quest of the officers, and nothing less than a very smart bonnet, indeed, or a really new muslin in a shop window, could recall them.
他们的目光立即在街上寻找军官，甚至一个非常时髦的帽子，或者一个真的新布料在商店的橱窗里，才能让他们回来。
But the attention of every lady was soon caught by a young man, whom they had never seen before, of most gentlemanlike appearance, walking with an officer on the other side of the way.
但每个女士很快就被一个年轻人吸引了，他以前从没见过，长相非常绅士，和军官在街的另一侧一起走。
The officer was the very Mr. Denny concerning whose return from London Lydia came to inquire, and he bowed as they passed.
军官是和莉迪亚从伦敦回来的，莉迪亚来打听他的归来，他向他们鞠躬。

All were struck with the stranger’s air, all wondered who he could be; and Kitty and Lydia, determined if possible to find out, led the way across the street, under pretence of wanting something in an opposite shop, and fortunately had just gained the pavement, when the two gentlemen, turning back, had reached the same spot.
所有人被这个陌生人的风度所吸引，所有人都想知道他是谁；凯蒂和莉迪亚，决心无论如何也要找到答案，带领他们穿过街道，假装要买东西，恰好到了人行道，当两位先生转身时，就到了同一个地方。

Mr. Denny addressed them directly, and entreated permission to introduce his friend, Mr. Wickham, who had returned with him the day before from town, and, he was happy to say, had accepted a commission in their corps.
丁内尔回头直接向他们打招呼，并恳请允许他引见他的朋友威克姆先生，威克姆先生前一天从镇上回来，丁内尔回家时也带回来了，而且他高兴地说，威克姆先生已经接受了他们的部队的任命。
This was exactly as it should be; for the young man wanted only regimentals to make him completely charming.
这样正好，因为年轻人只缺军装，就能完全迷人。
His appearance was greatly in his favour: he had all the best parts of beauty, a fine countenance, a good figure, and very pleasing address.
他的外表非常有利：他有所有美丽的好部分，一个漂亮的脸庞，一个好身材，非常令人愉快的举止。

The introduction was followed up on his side by a happy readiness of conversation—a readiness at the same time perfectly correct and unassuming; and the whole party were still standing and talking together very agreeably, when the sound of horses drew their notice, and Darcy and Bingley were seen riding down the street.
这个介绍被他的谈话的快乐准备所跟随，同时他谈话的准备也完全正确，不显摆；整个队伍仍然站立和交谈，非常愉快，当马的声音吸引他们的注意时，达西和贝内特正在街上骑马。
On distinguishing the ladies of the group the two gentlemen came directly towards them, and began the usual civilities.
当他们辨认出团体中的女士时，两位先生直接向他们靠近，开始例行的礼貌。
Bingley was the principal spokesman, and Miss Bennet the principal object.
贝内特是主要发言人，简·班森是主要对象。
He was then, he said, on his way to Longbourn on purpose to inquire after her.
他说，他当时是去长隆恩去打听她的。

Mr. Darcy corroborated it with a bow, and was beginning to determine not to fix his eyes on Elizabeth, when they were suddenly arrested by the sight of the stranger; and Elizabeth happening to see the countenance of both as they looked at each other, was all astonishment at the effect of the meeting.
Darcy用一个鞠躬证实了这一点，正在决定不盯着伊丽莎白看，但被看到陌生人的脸时，他们突然被抓住，伊丽莎白看到他们互相看时，完全惊讶于相遇的效果。
Both changed colour, one looked white, the other red.
他们都变了颜色，一个苍白，另一个红。
Mr. Wickham, after a few moments, touched his hat—a salutation which Mr. Darcy just deigned to return.
威克汉姆先生，过了一会儿，他摘下帽子——这是达西先生仅勉强还礼。
What could be the meaning of it?
这是什么意思？
It was impossible to imagine; it was impossible not to long to know.
无法想象；无法不去想。
In another minute Mr. Bingley, but without seeming to have noticed what passed, took leave and rode on with his friend.
另外一分钟，比奇利先生，但似乎没有注意到什么，带着朋友离开，骑马去了。

Mr. Denny and Mr. Wickham walked with the young ladies to the door of Mr. Philips’s house, and then made their bows, in spite of Miss Lydia’s pressing entreaties that they would come in, and even in spite of Mrs. Philips’s throwing up the parlour window, and loudly seconding the invitation.
达登先生和威克汉姆先生和年轻小姐们走到菲利普斯先生家门前，然后向门行礼，尽管莉迪亚极力要求他们进来，甚至在莉迪亚的强烈要求下，菲利普斯太太甚至把客厅的窗户打开，大声邀请他们进来。

Mrs. Philips was always glad to see her nieces; and the two eldest, from their recent absence, were particularly welcome; and she was eagerly expressing her surprise at their sudden return home, which, as their own carriage had not fetched them, she should have known nothing about, if she had not happened to see Mr. Jones’s shopboy in the street, who had told her that they were not to send any more draughts to Netherfield, because the Miss Bennets were come away, when her civility was claimed towards Mr. Collins by Jane’s introduction of him.
菲利普斯太太总是很高兴见到她的侄女，两个最年长的，因为最近的缺席，特别受欢迎；而且她非常惊讶她们突然回家，她应该不知道，除非她没有看到在街上遇见的约翰逊先生的店员，他告诉她她们不再寄发到诺顿菲尔德，因为贝内特小姐们已经离开，当她的礼貌被简小姐的介绍而得到Jane的介绍。

She received him with her very best politeness, which he returned with as much more, apologizing for his intrusion, without any previous acquaintance with her, which he could not help flattering himself, however, might be justified by his relationship to the young ladies who introduced him to her notice.
她以她最好的礼貌接待他，他以更多的礼貌回报，为他的入侵道歉，尽管他不能不为他与年轻小姐们介绍他而感到得意，然而，他可能被他的关系到她们的注意。

Mrs. Philips was quite awed by such an excess of good breeding; but her contemplation of one stranger was soon put an end to by exclamations and inquiries about the other, of whom, however, she could only tell her nieces what they already knew, that Mr. Denny had brought him from London, and that he was to have a lieutenant’s commission in the ——shire.
菲利普斯太太非常敬畏这种过度的礼貌，但她的对一个陌生人的观察很快被对另一个的惊叹和询问所打断，她只能告诉她的侄女，约翰逊先生从伦敦带他来，他将得到一个——郡的上尉的委任。

She had been watching him the last hour, she said, as he walked up and down the street,—and had Mr. Wickham appeared, Kitty and Lydia would certainly have continued the occupation; but unluckily no one passed the windows now except a few of the officers, who, in comparison with the stranger, were become “stupid, disagreeable fellows.”
她说她一直在观察他，他说，当他走来走去的街道上，威克汉姆先生出现，凯蒂和莉迪亚肯定会继续这个活动；不幸的是现在只有少数军官经过窗户，他们与陌生人的比较变得“愚蠢、不愉快的家伙”。

Some of them were to dine with the Philipses the next day, and their aunt promised to make her husband call on Mr. Wickham, and give him an invitation also, if the family from Longbourn would come in the evening.
他们第二天将与菲利普斯太太一起吃饭，她的婶婶承诺叫菲利普斯先生和他一起邀请威克汉姆先生，如果诺顿菲尔德的家庭晚上来。
This was agreed to; and Mrs. Philips protested that they would have a nice comfortable noisy game of lottery tickets, and a little bit of hot supper afterwards.
这被同意了；菲利普斯太太抗议说，他们将有一个舒适的热闹的抽奖游戏，和一顿热的晚饭。
The prospect of such delights was very cheering, and they parted in mutual good spirits.
这样的欢乐是令人振奋的，他们互相友好地分手。
Mr. Collins repeated his apologies in quitting the room, and was assured, with unwearying civility, that they were perfectly needless.
达西先生在离开房间时重复他的道歉，并被保证，他们完全不需要。
