As they walked home, Elizabeth related to Jane what she had seen pass between the two gentlemen; but though Jane would have defended either or both, had they appeared to be wrong, she could no more explain such behaviour than her sister.
当他们回家时，伊丽莎白向简小姐讲述了她看到的两个绅士之间的行为；尽管简小姐会为他们中的任何一个或两个辩护，如果他们看起来是错误的，她无法解释这种行为，就像她的姐姐一样。
Mr. Collins on his return highly gratified Mrs. Bennet by admiring Mrs. Philips’s manners and politeness.
达西先生在返回时，对贝内特太太大加赞赏，她的礼貌和礼貌。

He protested that, except Lady Catherine and her daughter, he had never seen a more elegant woman; for she had not only received him with the utmost civility, but had even pointedly included him in her invitation for the next evening, although utterly unknown to her before.
他抗议说，除了达西夫人和她女儿之外，他从未见过如此优雅的女性；因为她不仅对他以最礼貌的态度接待，还特意邀请他参加下一次晚宴，尽管在此之前完全不认识她。
Something, he supposed, might be attributed to his connection with them, but yet he had never met with so much attention in the whole course of his life.
他觉得，这可能归因于他的关系，但无论如何，他一生中从未见过如此多的关注。

As no objection was made to the young people’s engagement with their aunt, and all Mr. Collins’s scruples of leaving Mr. and Mrs. Bennet for a single evening during his visit were most steadily resisted, the coach conveyed him and his five cousins at a suitable hour to Meryton; and the girls had the pleasure of hearing, as they entered the drawing-room, that Mr. Wickham had accepted their uncle’s invitation, and was then in the house.
当没有反对年轻人与表姐的婚事时，以及所有对马尔科姆先生离开贝内特夫妇的单晚拜访的顾虑都被彻底抵制时，马尔科姆先生和他的五个表兄弟在合适的时刻被马尔科姆先生的阿姨接到了米尔顿。当女孩们进入客厅时，他们听到马尔科姆先生已经接受了威克姆先生的邀请，并且正在家中。

When this information was given, and they had all taken their seats, Mr. Collins was at leisure to look around him and admire, and he was so much struck with the size and furniture of the apartment, that he declared he might almost have supposed himself in the small summer breakfast parlour at Rosings; a comparison that did not at first convey much gratification; but when Mrs. Philips understood from him what Rosings was, and who was its proprietor, when she had listened to the description of only one of Lady Catherine’s drawing-rooms, and found that the chimney-piece alone had cost eight hundred pounds, she felt all the force of the compliment, and would hardly have resented a comparison with the housekeeper’s room.
当这一信息传达出来，他们坐定之后，克林顿先生便有空闲四处打量，欣赏一番，他被房间的大小和家具所打动，几乎可以想象自己置身于罗瑟琳斯的小夏季度餐室中；这个比较起初并没有带来多少愉悦感；但当菲斯米尔太太从他口中得知罗瑟琳斯是什么样子，以及它的主人是谁，当她听了罗瑟琳斯的一间画室的描述，发现仅是壁炉架就花费了八百镑之后，她便体会到了这个恭维的全部含义，甚至几乎不会因为与管家的房间相比而感到不满。

In describing to her all the grandeur of Lady Catherine and her mansion, with occasional digressions in praise of his own humble abode, and the improvements it was receiving, he was happily employed until the gentlemen joined them; and he found in Mrs. Philips a very attentive listener, whose opinion of his consequence increased with what she heard, and who was resolving to retail it all among her neighbours as soon as she could.
他向她描述了所有罗森斯的宏伟，偶尔在赞美他自己的简陋住所，以及它正在接受的改进，他直到绅士们加入他们时才开始工作，他发现菲利普小姐是一个非常注意的听众，她对他的地位的了解随着她听到的而增加，她很快决定在她可以时将这个信息零售给她的邻居。

To the girls, who could not listen to their cousin, and who had nothing to do but to wish for an instrument, and examine their own indifferent imitations of china on the mantel-piece, the interval of waiting appeared very long.
对那些不能听他们表兄弟说话的女孩来说，等待的间隙似乎很长。
It was over at last, however.
然而，一切都结束了。

The gentlemen did approach: and when Mr. Wickham walked into the room, Elizabeth felt that she had neither been seeing him before, nor thinking of him since, with the smallest degree of unreasonable admiration.
男士们开始接近，当威克姆先生走进房间时，伊丽莎白感到她之前没有见过他，也没有对他的任何一点不合理的崇拜。

The officers of the ——shire were in general a very creditable, gentlemanlike set and the best of them were of the present party; but Mr. Wickham was as far beyond them all in person, countenance, air, and walk, as they were superior to the broad-faced stuffy uncle Philips, breathing port wine, who followed them into the room.
伯克郡的官员们通常是一个非常有荣誉的，绅士的群体，他们中的大多数是当前的队伍，但威克姆先生在体形、脸、风度和步态上都远远超过了他们，他们比宽脸的菲利普叔叔，喝着波特酒，跟随他们进入房间的人，要优越得多。

Mr. Wickham was the happy man towards whom almost every female eye was turned, and Elizabeth was the happy woman by whom he finally seated himself; and the agreeable manner in which he immediately fell into conversation, though it was only on its being a wet night, and on the probability of a rainy season, made her feel that the commonest, dullest, most threadbare topic might be rendered interesting by the skill of the speaker.
威克姆先生是几乎每个女性眼睛都转向的对象，而伊丽莎白是最终坐下来的人，使她感到，即使是最普通、最无聊、最陈旧的话题，也可以通过说话者的技巧变得有趣。

With such rivals for the notice of the fair as Mr. Wickham and the officers, Mr. Collins seemed to sink into insignificance; to the young ladies he certainly was nothing; but he had still at intervals a kind listener in Mrs. Philips, and was, by her watchfulness, most abundantly supplied with coffee and muffin.
由于威克姆先生和军官们的注意，马尔科姆先生似乎变得微不足道，对年轻女士们来说，他没有任何东西；但他仍然在菲利普小姐那里有一个友好的听众，她通过听到他的情况，对他的重要性感到满意，她很快决定在她可以时将这个信息零售给她的邻居。
When the card tables were placed, he had an opportunity of obliging her, in return, by sitting down to whist.
当牌桌被放置时，他有机会回报她，坐在威斯汀和莉迪亚之间的桥牌。

“I know little of the game at present,” said he, “but I shall be glad to improve myself; for in my situation of life——” Mrs. Philips was very thankful for his compliance, but could not wait for his reason.
“我目前对这个游戏了解不多，”他说，“但我很高兴能提高自己；因为我目前的生活——”菲利普小姐非常感谢他的同意，但她不能等待他的理由。
Mr. Wickham did not play at whist, and with ready delight was he received at the other table between Elizabeth and Lydia.
威克姆先生不玩桥牌，他很快乐地被接在伊丽莎白和莉迪亚之间的另一张桌子。

At first there seemed danger of Lydia’s engrossing him entirely, for she was a most determined talker; but being likewise extremely fond of lottery tickets, she soon grew too much interested in the game, too eager in making bets and exclaiming after prizes, to have attention for anyone in particular.
当最初似乎有莉迪亚会完全吸引他时，因为她是极其善于说话的，但同时她也非常喜欢彩票，她很快对游戏变得太过于投入，对赌注和对奖品的欢呼，以至于没有对任何人特别感兴趣。

Allowing for the common demands of the game, Mr. Wickham was therefore at leisure to talk to Elizabeth, and she was very willing to hear him, though what she chiefly wished to hear she could not hope to be told, the history of his acquaintance with Mr. Darcy.
除了游戏的常见要求，威克姆先生因此有时间与伊丽莎白交谈，她非常愿意听他说话，尽管她最希望听到的她不可能被告诉，关于她与达西先生的友谊的历史。
She dared not even mention that gentleman.
她甚至不敢提到那位先生。
Her curiosity, however, was unexpectedly relieved.
她的好奇心却意外地得到了缓解。
Mr. Wickham began the subject himself.
沃辛姆先生自己挑起了这个话题。
He inquired how far Netherfield was from Meryton; and, after receiving her answer, asked in a hesitating manner how long Mr. Darcy had been staying there.
他询问了诺顿与米尔登之间的距离，然后询问了查尔斯先生在那里的停留时间。
“About a month,” said Elizabeth; and then, unwilling to let the subject drop, added, “he is a man of very large property in Derbyshire, I understand.”
“大约一个月，”伊丽莎白说，然后不愿意放弃这个话题，补充道，“他是在德比郡拥有很大财产的人，我听说。”
“Yes,” replied Wickham; “his estate there is a noble one.
“是的，”沃辛姆说，“他的那块地产是一个非常大的地产。
A clear ten thousand per annum.
一笔十万年。
You could not have met with a person more capable of giving you certain information on that head than myself—for I have been connected with his family, in a particular manner, from my infancy.”
你不可能遇到一个比我自己更能够提供关于这方面信息的人的，因为我从小就是与他的家族有密切关系的。
Elizabeth could not but look surprised.
伊丽莎白无法不感到惊讶。
“You may well be surprised, Miss Bennet, at such an assertion, after seeing, as you probably might, the very cold manner of our meeting yesterday.
“你可能对这样的断言感到惊讶，简·班纳特小姐，因为昨天你可能看到我们见面时的非常冷淡的态度。
Are you much acquainted with Mr. Darcy?”
你对查尔斯先生很熟悉吗？”
“As much as I ever wish to be,” cried Elizabeth, warmly.
“我想要知道的越多越好，”伊丽莎白热情地说。
“I have spent four days in the same house with him, and I think him very disagreeable.”
“我在这座房子里与他共度了四天，我认为他很不讨人喜欢。”
“I have no right to give my opinion,” said Wickham, “as to his being agreeable or otherwise.
“我没有权利发表意见，因为关于他的是否愉快，我不能说。”
I am not qualified to form one.
我没有资格形成一个意见。
I have known him too long and too well to be a fair judge.
我知道他太久了，太了解了，不能成为一个公正的评判者。
It is impossible for me to be impartial.
我无法保持中立。
But I believe your opinion of him would in general astonish—and, perhaps, you would not express it quite so strongly anywhere else.
但我相信，你对他的看法在一般情况下会令人惊讶——也许，你不会在其他地方表达得那么强烈。
Here you are in your own family.”
你是在你自己的家族。
“Upon my word I say no more here than I might say in any house in the neighbourhood, except Netherfield.
“我保证，我在这里说的和在任何邻近的房子里说的差不多，除了诺顿菲尔德。
He is not at all liked in Hertfordshire.
他在赫特福德郡并不受人欢迎。
Everybody is disgusted with his pride.
人人都对他的骄傲感到厌恶。
You will not find him more favourably spoken of by anyone.”
你不会有人更喜欢他。
“I cannot pretend to be sorry,” said Wickham, after a short interruption, “that he or that any man should not be estimated beyond their deserts; but with him I believe it does not often happen.
“我不能假装为他难过，”威克汉姆在短暂的中断后说，“他或任何人在不应得到应得的评价，但对我来说，这并不经常发生。
The world is blinded by his fortune and consequence, or frightened by his high and imposing manners, and sees him only as he chooses to be seen.”
世界被他的财富和地位所蒙蔽，或被他的高傲和令人敬畏的举止所吓到，只看到他选择看到的样子。
“I should take him, even on my slight acquaintance, to be an ill-tempered man.”
“我应该把他，即使在我微薄的了解下，认为是一个脾气暴躁的人。
Wickham only shook his head.
威克汉姆只是摇头。
“I wonder,” said he, at the next opportunity of speaking, “whether he is likely to be in this country much longer.”
“我想，”他说，下一次有机会说话时，“他是否有可能在这一地区呆很长时间。
“I do not at all know; but I heard nothing of his going away when I was at Netherfield.
“我不知道，但我听说，在我离开诺顿菲尔德时，没有人提到他离开。
I hope your plans in favour of the ——shire will not be affected by his being in the neighbourhood.”
我希望你的对——郡的计划不会因为他的在附近而受到影响。
“Oh no—it is not for me to be driven away by Mr. Darcy.
“哦，不，我不被德雷克先生驱逐。
If he wishes to avoid seeing me he must go.
如果他希望避开我，就必须离开。

We are not on friendly terms, and it always gives me pain to meet him, but I have no reason for avoiding him but what I might proclaim to all the world—a sense of very great ill-usage, and most painful regrets at his being what he is.
我们并不友好，见到他总让我痛苦，但我不避讳他，只是因为我觉得受到了非常大的不公，并且非常痛苦地怀念他过去的父亲。

His father, Miss Bennet, the late Mr. Darcy, was one of the best men that ever breathed, and the truest friend I ever had; and I can never be in company with this Mr. Darcy without being grieved to the soul by a thousand tender recollections.
我的表姐简·贝内特，也就是那位已故的达西先生，是一位最好的男人，而且是我一生中最好的朋友；我永远无法在与达西先生在一起时感到快乐，因为我会想起许多温馨的回忆。
His behaviour to myself has been scandalous; but I verily believe I could forgive him anything and everything, rather than his disappointing the hopes and disgracing the memory of his father.”
他对我的行为是极其不公的；但我相信，我能够原谅他任何事情，甚至他的不公对待我的父亲。
Elizabeth found the interest of the subject increase, and listened with all her heart; but the delicacy of it prevented further inquiry.
詹姆斯发现这个话题引起了他的兴趣，并全心全意地听，但其复杂性阻止了进一步的探究。

Mr. Wickham began to speak on more general topics, Meryton, the neighbourhood, the society, appearing highly pleased with all that he had yet seen, and speaking of the latter, especially, with gentle but very intelligible gallantry.
弗利克汉姆开始谈论更广泛的话题，比如米尔顿镇，邻里，社会，他似乎对所见到的一切都感到非常满意，并且特别提到后者，尤其是，他以非常温柔但非常清晰的礼貌来谈论。
“It was the prospect of constant society, and good society,” he added, “which was my chief inducement to enter the ——shire.
“这是恒常的社交和良好的社交，”他补充道，“这是我进入——郡的主要动机。

I know it to be a most respectable, agreeable corps; and my friend Denny tempted me further by his account of their present quarters, and the very great attentions and excellent acquaintance Meryton had procured them.
我知道这是一个非常有尊重和愉快的队伍；我的朋友迪恩进一步诱惑我，通过他们的当前的地点和他们现在获得的非常高的注意和非常优秀的交往。
Society, I own, is necessary to me.
社会，我承认，对我来说是必要的。
I have been a disappointed man, and my spirits will not bear solitude.
我是一个失望的人，我的精神无法忍受孤独。
I must have employment and society.
我必须有工作和社交。
A military life is not what I was intended for, but circumstances have now made it eligible.
军队生活不适合我，但现在由于情况，它变得合适。

The church ought to have been my profession—I was brought up for the church; and I should at this time have been in possession of a most valuable living, had it pleased the gentleman we were speaking of just now.”
教会应该是我的职业，我被抚养长大是为教会；如果现在所说的那位先生高兴的话，我现在应该拥有一个非常有价值的职位。
“Indeed!”
“真的！”
“Yes—the late Mr. Darcy bequeathed me the next presentation of the best living in his gift.
“是的——已故的达西先生留给我下一个推荐的最好的职位。
He was my godfather, and excessively attached to me.
他是我的养父，对我过分依恋。
I cannot do justice to his kindness.
我无法公正地表达他的善良。
He meant to provide for me amply, and thought he had done it; but when the living fell, it was given elsewhere.”
他本打算给我提供充分的照顾，但当生活结束时，却给了别人。
“Good heavens!” cried Elizabeth; “but how could that be?
“天啊！”伊丽莎白惊呼，“怎么会这样？
How could his will be disregarded?
他的意志怎么能被忽视？
Why did not you seek legal redress?”
为什么不寻求法律救济？
“There was just such an informality in the terms of the bequest as to give me no hope from law.
“那遗嘱的措辞太随便了，让我没有希望通过法律来解决。

A man of honour could not have doubted the intention, but Mr. Darcy chose to doubt it—or to treat it as a merely conditional recommendation, and to assert that I had forfeited all claim to it by extravagance, imprudence, in short, anything or nothing.
一个有荣誉的人不会怀疑他的意图，但达西先生选择怀疑它——或者把它当作一个仅仅有条件的建议，并声称我因为奢侈、不理智等任何理由都没有资格得到它。

Certain it is that the living became vacant two years ago, exactly as I was of an age to hold it, and that it was given to another man; and no less certain is it, that I cannot accuse myself of having really done anything to deserve to lose it.
无疑，那活着的人在两年前就空缺了，正好和我应该拥有它的时候一样，而且那活人被另一个男人继承了；而且毫无疑问，我不能指责自己真的做了什么值得失去它的事情。
I have a warm unguarded temper, and I may perhaps have sometimes spoken my opinion of him, and to him, too freely.
我有热情的、不加掩饰的脾气，或许我曾经过于自由地表达过我对他的看法和对他说话。
I can recall nothing worse.
我可以回忆起一些更糟糕的事情。
But the fact is, that we are very different sort of men, and that he hates me.”
但事实是，我们是两种不同的男人，他讨厌我。
“This is quite shocking!
“这真是令人震惊！
He deserves to be publicly disgraced.”
他应该被公开羞辱。
“Some time or other he will be—but it shall not be by me.
“有一天他将会，但不会是我来羞辱他。”
Till I can forget his father, I can never defy or expose him.”
直到我能忘掉他父亲，我才永远不会违抗或揭露他。
Elizabeth honoured him for such feelings, and thought him handsomer than ever as he expressed them.
莉莎伊尔对他感到如此感情，而且认为他表达这些感情时更漂亮了。
“But what,” said she, after a pause, “can have been his motive? what can have induced him to behave so cruelly?”
“但是，什么，”她停顿了一下，说，“他有什么动机？什么使他如此残酷地表现出来？”
“A thorough, determined dislike of me—a dislike which I cannot but attribute in some measure to jealousy.
“一种彻底、坚定的厌恶，一种我不能不把部分归咎于嫉妒的厌恶。
Had the late Mr. Darcy liked me less, his son might have borne with me better; but his father’s uncommon attachment to me irritated him, I believe, very early in life.
如果晚年的先生不喜欢我，他的儿子可能会对我更宽容；但是他的父亲对我的特别的喜欢，引起了他很早的厌恶。
He had not a temper to bear the sort of competition in which we stood—the sort of preference which was often given me.”
他没有一种能忍受我们之间的竞争的脾气，也没有一种给予我特别的偏爱的倾向。

“I had not thought Mr. Darcy so bad as this—though I have never liked him, I had not thought so very ill of him—I had supposed him to be despising his fellow-creatures in general, but did not suspect him of descending to such malicious revenge, such injustice, such inhumanity as this!”
“我没想到先生这么坏，虽然我从未喜欢他，我没想到这么坏；我没想到他把他的同胞们看作是不好的，但我没有怀疑他把他的同胞们看作是不好的，我怀疑他把他的同胞们看作是不好的，我怀疑他把他的同胞们看作是不好的。”
After a few minutes’ reflection, however, she continued, “I do remember his boasting one day, at Netherfield, of the implacability of his resentments, of his having an unforgiving temper.
他没有一种能忍受我们之间的竞争的脾气，也没有一种给予我特别的偏爱的倾向。
His disposition must be dreadful.”
他的性格一定很可怕。
“I will not trust myself on the subject,” replied Wickham; “I can hardly be just to him.”
“我不会信任自己去讨论这个问题，”韦奇霍尔姆说，“我很难对他说公正。”
Elizabeth was again deep in thought, and after a time exclaimed, “To treat in such a manner the godson, the friend, the favourite of his father!”
莉莎伊尔再次陷入深思，过了一会儿，她叫道：“对这样对待他的神子，他的朋友，他的父亲的最爱的人！”
She could have added, “A young man, too, like you, whose very countenance may vouch for your being amiable.”
她可以补充说：“一个年轻人，像你一样，你那年轻的脸孔可以证明你是一个友善的人。”
But she contented herself with—“And one, too, who had probably been his own companion from childhood, connected together, as I think you said, in the closest manner.”
但她满足于——“而且，一个，也是，一个可能是他自己的同伴从童年起就在一起的人，我猜想你所说的，关系最紧密的人。”
“We were born in the same parish, within the same park; the greatest part of our youth was passed together: inmates of the same house, sharing the same amusements, objects of the same parental care.
“我们是在同一个教区出生的，同一个公园里长大的；我们大部分的青春是在一起度过的：我们住在一个同一个地方，共享同样的娱乐，同样的父母的关怀。

My father began life in the profession which your uncle, Mr. Philips, appears to do so much credit to; but he gave up everything to be of use to the late Mr. Darcy, and devoted all his time to the care of the Pemberley property.
我父亲开始时从事的行业，你的叔叔菲利普斯先生似乎为他大大增光，但他放弃了一切来对已故的达西先生有所贡献，全身心地投入到佩茅尔地产的照料上。
He was most highly esteemed by Mr. Darcy, a most intimate, confidential friend.
他深得达西先生的敬重，达西先生是他最亲密、最信任的朋友。

Mr. Darcy often acknowledged himself to be under the greatest obligations to my father’s active superintendence; and when, immediately before my father’s death, Mr. Darcy gave him a voluntary promise of providing for me, I am convinced that he felt it to be as much a debt of gratitude to him as of affection to myself.”
达西先生常常承认自己深受我父亲积极监督之恩；而在我父亲临终前，达西先生自愿答应给我提供生活费之时，我确信他感到对我的感激之情犹如对我自己的感情一样深厚。
“How strange!” cried Elizabeth.
“奇怪！” Elizabeth 惊呼。
“How abominable!
多么可恶啊！
I wonder that the very pride of this Mr. Darcy has not made him just to you.
我想这个戴奇先生的骄傲难道没有使他对你变得公正。
If from no better motive, that he should not have been too proud to be dishonest,—for dishonesty I must call it.”
如果并非出于更好的动机，他就不应该太骄傲而不诚实——在我看来，我必须把它叫做不诚实。
“It is wonderful,” replied Wickham; “for almost all his actions may be traced to pride; and pride has often been his best friend.
它倒是 wonderful，威克姆回答说，因为他的几乎所有的行为都可以归因于骄傲，而骄傲常常是他最好的朋友。
It has connected him nearer with virtue than any other feeling.
它使他与美德的关系比任何其他情感都更亲近。
But we are none of us consistent; and in his behaviour to me there were stronger impulses even than pride.”
但我们都 inconsistency；对他对我 behaviour 中更强的冲动甚至超过骄傲。
“Can such abominable pride as his have ever done him good?”
他那样的可憎骄傲难道曾经对他有过好处？
“Yes; it has often led him to be liberal and generous; to give his money freely, to display hospitality, to assist his tenants, and relieve the poor.

是的；它 often 曾经 常常 引导 他 使他 使他 使他 使他 使他 使他 使他 使他 使他 使他 使他 使他 使他 使他 使他 使他 使他 使他 使他 使他 使他 使他 使他 使他 使他 使他 使他 使他 使他 使他 使他 使他 使他 使他 使他 使他 使他 使他 使他 使他 使他 使他 使他 使他 使他 使他 使他 使他 使他 使他 使他 使他 使他 使他 使他 使他 使他 使他 使他 使他 使他 使他 使他 使他 使他 使他 使他 使他 使他 使他 使他 使他 使他 使他 使他 使他 使他 使他 使他 使他 使他 使他 使他 使他 使他 使他 使他 使他 使他 使他 使他 使他 使他 使他
Family pride, and filial pride, for he is very proud of what his father was, have done this.
家族的骄傲，以及对父辈的骄傲，因为他非常自豪于他父亲所为，这都促成了此事。
Not to appear to disgrace his family, to degenerate from the popular qualities, or lose the influence of the Pemberley House, is a powerful motive.
不致于显得辱没他的家族，不堕落为大众所推崇的品质，也不失去彭伯里府的影响，这是强有力的动机。

He has also brotherly pride, which, with some brotherly affection, makes him a very kind and careful guardian of his sister; and you will hear him generally cried up as the most attentive and best of brothers.”
他还有兄长的骄傲，这种骄傲与一些兄长的亲昵，使他成为一位非常亲切细心的妹妹监护人；你也会经常听到他被称赞为最细心、最好的哥哥。
“What sort of a girl is Miss Darcy?”
黛西小姐是什么样的女孩？
He shook his head.
他摇了摇头。
“I wish I could call her amiable.
“我希望我能称呼她友好。
It gives me pain to speak ill of a Darcy; but she is too much like her brother,—very, very proud.
说她不好的话让我感到痛苦，但她太像她的哥哥了——非常非常骄傲。
As a child, she was affectionate and pleasing, and extremely fond of me; and I have devoted hours and hours to her amusement.
她小时候很亲热和讨人喜欢，对我特别喜欢，我花了很多小时陪她玩。
But she is nothing to me now.
但现在她对我已经没有用了。
She is a handsome girl, about fifteen or sixteen, and, I understand, highly accomplished.
她是个漂亮女孩，大约十五六岁，据说很会做派。
Since her father’s death her home has been London, where a lady lives with her, and superintends her education.”
自父亲去世后，她的家一直在伦敦，有一位女士住在她身边，负责她的教育。
After many pauses and many trials of other subjects, Elizabeth could not help reverting once more to the first, and saying,—
经过了许多停顿和尝试其他话题，伊丽莎白忍不住再次回到最初的话题，并说——
“I am astonished at his intimacy with Mr. Bingley.
“我对他的亲近Mr. Bingley感到惊讶。
How can Mr. Bingley, who seems good-humour itself, and is, I really believe, truly amiable, be in friendship with such a man?
Mr. Bingley看起来很友好，我相信他确实很友好，怎么会和这样的男人结交？
How can they suit each other?
他们怎么能够互相匹配？
Do you know Mr. Bingley?”
你知道Mr. Bingley吗？
“Not at all.”
“一点也不知道。”
“He is a sweet-tempered, amiable, charming man.
“他是一个温和、友好的、迷人的男人。
He cannot know what Mr. Darcy is.”
他不知道Mr. Darcy是什么样的人。”
“Probably not; but Mr. Darcy can please where he chooses.
他并不需要能力。
He does not want abilities.
他可以成为一个值得交谈的伴侣，只要他认为值得。
He can be a conversible companion if he thinks it worth his while.
与那些在他等同的富人相比，他是个非常不同的男人。
Among those who are at all his equals in consequence, he is a very different man from what he is to the less prosperous.
他的骄傲从不抛弃他；但是与富人打交道时，他慷慨大方，公正，真诚，理性和正直，而且也许还很讨人喜欢——当然，考虑到财富和地位。
His pride never deserts him; but with the rich he is liberal-minded, just, sincere, rational, honourable, and, perhaps, agreeable,—allowing something for fortune and figure.”
他知道自己很清楚，女士，当人们坐到牌桌前时，他们必须接受这些事情的不确定性——幸运的是，我并不处于那种需要考虑五先令重要性的境地。
The whist party soon afterwards breaking up, the players gathered round the other table, and Mr. Collins took his station between his cousin Elizabeth and Mrs. Philips.
卡尔文·德·布尔戈夫人很快解散了牌桌上的游戏，玩家们聚集在另一张桌子旁，而柯林斯先生则站在他的表姐伊丽莎白和菲利普夫人之间。
The usual inquiries as to his success were made by the latter.
他向后者询问了关于他成功的常规问题。

It had not been very great; he had lost every point; but when Mrs. Philips began to express her concern thereupon, he assured her, with much earnest gravity, that it was not of the least importance; that he considered the money as a mere trifle, and begged she would not make herself uneasy.
这并不大，他输了所有的点数，但当菲利普夫人开始表达她的担忧时，他向她保证，带着很大的严肃，说这并不重要，他认为钱只是微不足道的，请求她不要让自己感到不安。

“I know very well, madam,” said he, “that when persons sit down to a card table they must take their chance of these things,—and happily I am not in such circumstances as to make five shillings any object.
“我当然知道，女士，当人们坐到牌桌前时，他们必须接受这些事情的不确定性——幸运的是，我并不处于那种需要考虑五先令重要性的境地。
There are, undoubtedly, many who could not say the same; but, thanks to Lady Catherine de Bourgh, I am removed far beyond the necessity of regarding little matters.”
无疑有很多人不能说同样的话，但要感谢卡特赖特·德·布尔戈夫人，我已经远离了对小事的考虑。

Mr. Wickham’s attention was caught; and after observing Mr. Collins for a few moments, he asked Elizabeth in a low voice whether her relations were very intimately acquainted with the family of De Bourgh.
沃克汉姆先生的注意力被吸引过来，然后观察了柯林斯先生几分钟，然后低声问道，伊丽莎白小姐，她的亲戚与布尔戈夫人家族的关系非常亲密吗？
“Lady Catherine de Bourgh,” she replied, “has very lately given him a living.
“卡特赖特·德·布尔戈夫人，”她回答，“最近给了他一个职位。
I hardly know how Mr. Collins was first introduced to her notice, but he certainly has not known her long.”
我并不知道柯林斯先生是如何第一次被她注意到的，但他肯定没有很久。
“You know of course that Lady Catherine de Bourgh and Lady Anne Darcy were sisters; consequently that she is aunt to the present Mr. Darcy.”
“当然，女士，您知道，卡特赖特·德·布尔戈夫人和安妮·德·卡特赖特是姐妹，所以她是目前的德·卡特赖特先生的姑姑。
“No, indeed, I did not.
“不，当然，我并没有。
I knew nothing at all of Lady Catherine’s connections.
我对达西夫人和达西小姐的任何关系一无所知。
I never heard of her existence till the day before yesterday.”
我直到前天才听说她的存在。
“Her daughter, Miss de Bourgh, will have a very large fortune, and it is believed that she and her cousin will unite the two estates.”
“达西小姐，德伯格小姐，将会拥有一个巨大的财富，而且据说她和她的堂兄将会把两个庄园合并起来。”
This information made Elizabeth smile, as she thought of poor Miss Bingley.
这些信息让伊丽莎白微笑，因为她想起了可怜的贝金莱小姐。
Vain indeed must be all her attentions, vain and useless her affection for his sister and her praise of himself, if he were already self-destined to another.
如果他现在注定要嫁给别人，那么他所有的注意和对姐姐的爱以及对他的夸奖，都是徒劳的。

“Mr. Collins,” said she, “speaks highly both of Lady Catherine and her daughter; but, from some particulars that he has related of her Ladyship, I suspect his gratitude misleads him; and that, in spite of her being his patroness, she is an arrogant, conceited woman.”
“我先生，”她说道，“对达西夫人和她的女儿说的都是好话，但，从他提到她的情况来看，我怀疑他的感激心误导了他；而且，尽管她是他的保护者，她是一个傲慢、自负的女人。”

“I believe her to be both in a great degree,” replied Wickham; “I have not seen her for many years; but I very well remember that I never liked her, and that her manners were dictatorial and insolent.
“我先生，”韦奇姆说道，“说达西夫人和她的女儿都很出色，但我怀疑他的感激心误导了他；而且，尽管她是他的保护者，她是一个傲慢、自负的女人。”

She has the reputation of being remarkably sensible and clever; but I rather believe she derives part of her abilities from her rank and fortune, part from her authoritative manner, and the rest from the pride of her nephew, who chooses that everyone connected with him should have an understanding of the first class.”
她有良好的声誉，聪明而有见识；但我相信她的一部分才能来自她的地位和财富，一部分来自她傲慢的举止，其余来自她侄子的骄傲，他选择每个人都了解第一等级的人。”

Elizabeth allowed that he had given a very rational account of it, and they continued talking together with mutual satisfaction till supper put an end to cards, and gave the rest of the ladies their share of Mr. Wickham’s attentions.
伊丽莎白同意他给出一个非常合理的解释，并且他们继续交谈，互相满意，直到晚餐结束，卡牌游戏结束，给了长门庄园的女士们一些他们自己的Mr. Wickham的注意。
There could be no conversation in the noise of Mrs. Philips’s supper party, but his manners recommended him to everybody.
在米歇尔太太的晚餐会上，没有任何谈话，但他的举止推荐他给每个人。
Whatever he said, was said well; and whatever he did, done gracefully.
无论他说什么，说得都很好；无论他做什么，做得都很优雅。
Elizabeth went away with her head full of him.
伊丽莎白带着满脑子的他。

She could think of nothing but of Mr. Wickham, and of what he had told her, all the way home; but there was not time for her even to mention his name as they went, for neither Lydia nor Mr. Collins were once silent.
无论他说什么，说什么都很好；无论他做什么，做什么都优雅。

Lydia talked incessantly of lottery tickets, of the fish she had lost and the fish she had won; and Mr. Collins, in describing the civility of Mr. and Mrs. Philips, protesting that he did not in the least regard his losses at whist, enumerating all the dishes at supper, and repeatedly fearing that he crowded his cousins, had more to say than he could well manage before the carriage stopped at Longbourn House.
莱西娅不停地谈论彩票，鱼的损失和鱼的赢利；而柯林斯先生，描述菲利普夫妇的礼貌，抗议他一点也不在乎他的卡牌损失，列举了晚餐的所有菜肴，并反复担心他超过了他的亲戚，先生们，车停在长门庄园。
Elizabeth related to Jane, the next day, what had passed between Mr. Wickham and herself.
杰斯宾第二天就向简讲述了与威克姆先生之间的事情。

Jane listened with astonishment and concern: she knew not how to believe that Mr. Darcy could be so unworthy of Mr. Bingley’s regard; and yet it was not in her nature to question the veracity of a young man of such amiable appearance as Wickham.
简惊讶而忧虑地听着：她不知道如何相信威克姆先生对贝金赛尔的尊敬是不值得的；然而，她性格中不会怀疑一个如此善良的小伙子所说的话的真伪。

The possibility of his having really endured such unkindness was enough to interest all her tender feelings; and nothing therefore remained to be done but to think well of them both, to defend the conduct of each, and throw into the account of accident or mistake whatever could not be otherwise explained.
他可能真的遭受了如此的不公，这足以引起她所有温柔的感情；因此，唯一需要做的事情就是认为他们俩都好，为他们的行为辩护，并把无法解释的事故或错误归咎于它们。
“They have both,” said she, “been deceived, I dare say, in some way or other, of which we can form no idea.
“他们俩都”，她说道，“都被欺骗了，我想，可能会在某种方式上，我们无法想象。
Interested people have perhaps misrepresented each to the other.
有心人可能已经把他们俩误解了。
It is, in short, impossible for us to conjecture the causes or circumstances which may have alienated them, without actual blame on either side.”
短短一句话，我们无法推测他们之间可能产生的原因或情况，除非我们能够解释掉。
“Very true, indeed; and now, my dear Jane, what have you got to say in behalf of the interested people who have probably been concerned in the business?
“非常正确，确实如此；现在，亲爱的简，你们对那些可能涉及此事的有心人有什么要说的？
Do clear them, too, or we shall be obliged to think ill of somebody.”
也让他们澄清，否则我们就会认为某人不值得信任。
“Laugh as much as you choose, but you will not laugh me out of my opinion.
“你笑吧，但你不会把我不从心里说服。
My dearest Lizzy, do but consider in what a disgraceful light it places Mr. Darcy, to be treating his father’s favourite in such a manner,—one whom his father had promised to provide for.
我亲爱的简，你只要想想，把一个在你父亲的宠儿身上欺骗的先生放在一个不值得信任的人的脸上，这会把查尔斯先生放在什么样的不光彩的光线下。
It is impossible.
这是不可能的。
No man of common humanity, no man who had any value for his character, could be capable of it.
没有人，即使是普通人，也没有价值，谁会相信他的行为。
Can his most intimate friends be so excessively deceived in him?
他的最亲密的朋友会如此过度地欺骗他吗？
Oh no.”
哦，不。

“I can much more easily believe Mr. Bingley’s being imposed on than that Mr. Wickham should invent such a history of himself as he gave me last night; names, facts, everything mentioned without ceremony.
“我更能够相信贝金赛尔先生被欺骗，而不是威克姆先生会编造一个关于自己的一切都没有仪式的谎言；名字、事实、一切都没有仪式地提到。
If it be not so, let Mr. Darcy contradict it.
如果不是这样，让达西先生来反驳。
Besides, there was truth in his looks.”
除此之外，他的眼神里也有真挚。
“It is difficult, indeed—it is distressing.
“确实很难，真的很令人沮丧。
One does not know what to think.”
我们不知道应该怎样想。
“I beg your pardon;—one knows exactly what to think.”
“我向你道歉；——我完全知道应该怎样想。
But Jane could think with certainty on only one point,—that Mr. Bingley, if he had been imposed on, would have much to suffer when the affair became public.
只有简可以确定一件事——如果贝内特先生被欺骗，当这件事公之于众时，他会遭受很多痛苦。

The two young ladies were summoned from the shrubbery, where this conversation passed, by the arrival of some of the very persons of whom they had been speaking; Mr. Bingley and his sisters came to give their personal invitation for the long expected ball at Netherfield, which was fixed for the following Tuesday.
这两个年轻女士被召唤回到灌木丛中，这次谈话在那里进行，由贝内特先生和他的姐妹们来给期待已久的诺顿菲尔特的长舞会发出邀请，定于下星期二举行。
The two ladies were delighted to see their dear friend again, called it an age since they had met, and repeatedly asked what she had been doing with herself since their separation.
这两个女士再次见到他们的挚友，感到非常高兴，说起来已经很久没有见面了，多次询问她们分开后她自己做了什么。
To the rest of the family they paid little attention; avoiding Mrs. Bennet as much as possible, saying not much to Elizabeth, and nothing at all to the others.
对于家中的其他人，他们几乎没有注意；尽可能避开史密斯太太，对爱丽丝说不多，对其他人说很少。
They were soon gone again, rising from their seats with an activity which took their brother by surprise, and hurrying off as if eager to escape from Mrs. Bennet’s civilities.
他们很快又走开了，从座位上站起，以一种令哥哥惊讶的活动，匆匆离去，好像急于逃避史密斯太太的礼节。
The prospect of the Netherfield ball was extremely agreeable to every female of the family.
诺顿菲尔特的舞会对家中的每个女性来说都极其愉快。
Mrs. Bennet chose to consider it as given in compliment to her eldest daughter, and was particularly flattered by receiving the invitation from Mr. Bingley himself, instead of a ceremonious card.
老夫人认为这是对她大女儿的恭维，并且特别荣幸地收到了由贝内特先生本人发出的邀请，而不是一个正式的卡片。

Jane pictured to herself a happy evening in the society of her two friends, and the attentions of their brother; and Elizabeth thought with pleasure of dancing a great deal with Mr. Wickham, and of seeing a confirmation of everything in Mr. Darcy’s look and behaviour.
简想象到与她的两个朋友在一起的快乐夜晚，以及她哥哥的注意，她喜欢在舞会上跳舞很多，看到与达西先生的眼神和行为的确认。

The happiness anticipated by Catherine and Lydia depended less on any single event, or any particular person; for though they each, like Elizabeth, meant to dance half the evening with Mr. Wickham, he was by no means the only partner who could satisfy them, and a ball was, at any rate, a ball.
基特和丽莎的幸福预期依赖于任何单一事件或任何特定的人；因为尽管她们俩像爱丽丝一样打算在下午大部分时间里和威尔克斯姆一起跳舞，他并不是唯一可以满足她们的人，舞会至少是一个舞会。
And even Mary could assure her family that she had no disinclination for it.
而甚至玛丽也可以向她的家人保证她没有对舞会的任何不情愿。
“While I can have my mornings to myself,” said she, “it is enough.
我的早晨可以独享，她说，“这已经足够了。
I think it is no sacrifice to join occasionally in evening engagements.
我认为偶尔参加晚上的社交活动也是值得的。
Society has claims on us all; and I profess myself one of those who consider intervals of recreation and amusement as desirable for everybody.”
社会对我们每个人都有要求，我宣称自己是其中的一员，认为休闲和娱乐是每个人应该追求的。

Elizabeth’s spirits were so high on the occasion, that though she did not often speak unnecessarily to Mr. Collins, she could not help asking him whether he intended to accept Mr. Bingley’s invitation, and if he did, whether he would think it proper to join in the evening’s amusement; and she was rather surprised to find that he entertained no scruple whatever on that head, and was very far from dreading a rebuke, either from the Archbishop or Lady Catherine de Bourgh, by venturing to dance.
莉莉丝在那个场合的精神非常高涨，尽管她不经常无礼地与马修·柯林斯交谈，但她还是忍不住问他是否打算接受贝金赛尔先生的邀请，如果他接受的话，是否愿意参加晚上的娱乐活动；她惊讶地发现他对此毫无顾虑，甚至不害怕受到主教或德伯格夫人这样的人的责备，甚至在跳舞方面也没有顾虑。

“I am by no means of opinion, I assure you,” said he, “that a ball of this kind, given by a young man of character, to respectable people, can have any evil tendency; and I am so far from objecting to dancing myself, that I shall hope to be honoured with the hands of all my fair cousins in the course of the evening; and I take this opportunity of soliciting yours, Miss Elizabeth, for the two first dances especially; a preference which I trust my cousin Jane will attribute to the right cause, and not to any disrespect for her.”
“我可不这么认为，”他说，“这种规模的聚会，由一个有声望的年轻人举办，给有声望的人们，不会有什么坏的倾向；而且我一点也不反对跳舞，我希望在晚上的时候，我所有的漂亮表亲们都会被邀请，我希望我的表妹简也会把我的邀请视为正确的理由，而不是对我的轻视。”
Elizabeth felt herself completely taken in.
莉莉丝完全被吸引住了。
She had fully proposed being engaged by Wickham for those very dances; and to have Mr. Collins instead!—her liveliness had been never worse timed.
她已经完全提议要被威克汉姆选中参加那些晚上的舞蹈，而要得到马修·柯林斯的邀请！——她的机灵度正好在那个时刻到来。
There was no help for it, however.
无论如何，都无可奈何。
Mr. Wickham’s happiness and her own was perforce delayed a little longer, and Mr. Collins’s proposal accepted with as good a grace as she could.
威克汉姆的幸福和她的幸福是被迫推迟的，马修·柯林斯的提议被接受，就像她可以接受的最好的态度一样。
She was not the better pleased with his gallantry, from the idea it suggested of something more.
她对他的勇气并不满意，因为这暗示了更多的东西。

It now first struck her, that she was selected from among her sisters as worthy of being the mistress of Hunsford Parsonage, and of assisting to form a quadrille table at Rosings, in the absence of more eligible visitors.
这一点现在第一次让她意识到，她被选中作为赫恩福德庄园的主人，和罗森斯登的四行舞台，而没有更合适的客人。

The idea soon reached to conviction, as she observed his increasing civilities towards herself, and heard his frequent attempt at a compliment on her wit and vivacity; and though more astonished than gratified herself by this effect of her charms, it was not long before her mother gave her to understand that the probability of their marriage was exceedingly agreeable to her.
这个想法很快到达了意识，因为她观察到他的逐渐礼貌地对待自己，听到他频繁的尝试赞美她的机智和活力；尽管她自己感到惊讶而不是满足，但很快她母亲告诉她，婚姻的可能性对她来说非常愉快。
Elizabeth, however, did not choose to take the hint, being well aware that a serious dispute must be the consequence of any reply.
莉莉丝，然而，没有选择接受这个暗示，因为她很清楚，任何回复都会导致一场严肃的争论。
Mr. Collins might never make the offer, and, till he did, it was useless to quarrel about him.
马修·柯林斯可能永远不会提出这个提议，直到他提出，那么就没有什么值得争吵的了。

If there had not been a Netherfield ball to prepare for and talk of, the younger Miss Bennets would have been in a pitiable state at this time; for, from the day of the invitation to the day of the ball, there was such a succession of rain as prevented their walking to Meryton once.
如果没有一个诺顿菲尔德的舞会来准备和谈论，年轻的宾恩伯小姐们在这个时候会处于非常可怜的状态；因为从邀请到舞会，有一系列的雨阻止他们一次步行到米尔顿。
No aunt, no officers, no news could be sought after; the very shoe-roses for Netherfield were got by proxy.
没有姑妈，没有军官，没有消息可寻；连为纳特菲尔德准备的鞋带玫瑰也是托人捎来的。

Even Elizabeth might have found some trial of her patience in weather which totally suspended the improvement of her acquaintance with Mr. Wickham; and nothing less than a dance on Tuesday could have made such a Friday, Saturday, Sunday, and Monday endurable to Kitty and Lydia.
就连伊丽莎白也可能会在天气完全阻止她与弗吉尼亚的交往时找到一些对她的耐心的考验；甚至在星期二举行舞会，也根本无法让星期五、星期六、星期天和星期一变得令人忍受。
Till Elizabeth entered the drawing-room at Netherfield, and looked in vain for Mr. Wickham among the cluster of red coats there assembled, a doubt of his being present had never occurred to her.
到了伊丽莎白进入诺顿菲尔特的客厅时，她没有在聚集的红色军装中发现威克姆，她心中的疑虑从未出现过。
The certainty of meeting him had not been checked by any of those recollections that might not unreasonably have alarmed her.
与那些可能不合理的回忆不同，她对与他重逢的确定性没有受到任何影响。

She had dressed with more than usual care, and prepared in the highest spirits for the conquest of all that remained unsubdued of his heart, trusting that it was not more than might be won in the course of the evening.
她打扮得比平时更仔细，并且在最愉快的心情中准备了与他心爱的一切的征服，她相信在晚上他不会赢得太多。

But in an instant arose the dreadful suspicion of his being purposely omitted, for Mr. Darcy’s pleasure, in the Bingleys’ invitation to the officers; and though this was not exactly the case, the absolute fact of his absence was pronounced by his friend Mr. Denny, to whom Lydia eagerly applied, and who told them that Wickham had been obliged to go to town on business the day before, and was not yet returned; adding, with a significant smile,—
但瞬间出现了可怕的怀疑，因为威克姆被排除在外，因为贝金斯邀请军官们参加的聚会，而威克姆的缺席被他的朋友戴恩先生证实，戴恩先生告诉他们，威克姆因为前一天去镇上出差，还没有回来，还说，脸上带着意味深长的微笑——
“I do not imagine his business would have called him away just now, if he had not wished to avoid a certain gentleman here.”
“我不认为他的生意会叫他今天来，除非他不想见一个特定的先生。”

This part of his intelligence, though unheard by Lydia, was caught by Elizabeth; and, as it assured her that Darcy was not less answerable for Wickham’s absence than if her first surmise had been just, every feeling of displeasure against the former was so sharpened by immediate disappointment, that she could hardly reply with tolerable civility to the polite inquiries which he directly afterwards approached to make.
这部分的智慧虽然没有听给莉迪亚，却被伊丽莎白听到，并且，因为这表明威克姆的缺席不是因为她的最初猜测，所以她对威克姆的不满被立即的失望所加剧，以至于她几乎无法用礼貌的回应来回答他直接后来的询问。
Attention, forbearance, patience with Darcy, was injury to Wickham.
对威克姆的注意、忍耐、耐心是对他不忠的。

She was resolved against any sort of conversation with him, and turned away with a degree of ill-humour which she could not wholly surmount even in speaking to Mr. Bingley, whose blind partiality provoked her.
她决心不要与他交谈，当她转过身时，她无法完全克服对他的不耐烦，即使在与比内斯先生交谈时也是如此。

But Elizabeth was not formed for ill-humour; and though every prospect of her own was destroyed for the evening, it could not dwell long on her spirits; and, having told all her griefs to Charlotte Lucas, whom she had not seen for a week, she was soon able to make a voluntary transition to the oddities of her cousin, and to point him out to her particular notice.
但伊丽莎白不是脾气不好的人，尽管她所有的希望都破灭了，晚上也难以保持她的精神，她告诉了简·卢卡斯，她已经一个星期没有见到她，她很快就能够自愿过渡到她表弟的古怪之处，并指出他来注意。
The two first dances, however, brought a return of distress: they were dances of mortification.
但前两个舞会带来了痛苦的回响：它们是因羞耻而来的舞会。

Mr. Collins, awkward and solemn, apologizing instead of attending, and often moving wrong without being aware of it, gave her all the shame and misery which a disagreeable partner for a couple of dances can give.
威廉·康塞尔，笨拙而庄重，代替出席，经常移动错误，给了她所有的羞辱和痛苦，一个不讨人喜欢的舞伴可以给。
The moment of her release from him was ecstasy.
释放她的那一刻是狂喜。
She danced next with an officer, and had the refreshment of talking of Wickham, and of hearing that he was universally liked.
她在舞会上与一名军官跳舞，得到了与威克姆交谈的满足，并且听到他很受欢迎。

When those dances were over, she returned to Charlotte Lucas, and was in conversation with her, when she found herself suddenly addressed by Mr. Darcy, who took her so much by surprise in his application for her hand, that, without knowing what she did, she accepted him.
当那些舞会结束时，她回到了简·卢卡斯，与她交谈，当她发现自己突然被先生威克姆接洽时，她被他如此突然的求婚所震惊，以至于她没有知道她做了什么，她接受了他。
He walked away again immediately, and she was left to fret over her own want of presence of mind: Charlotte tried to console her.
他立即走开了，她被留了下来，为自己的缺乏机智而烦恼：简·卢卡斯试图安慰她。
“I dare say you will find him very agreeable.”
“我敢说你会觉得他很讨人喜欢。”
“Heaven forbid!
“天啊！
That would be the greatest misfortune of all!
这才真是最大的不幸！
To find a man agreeable whom one is determined to hate!
要找到一个自己决定要讨厌的人，却偏偏要讨人喜欢！
Do not wish me such an evil.”
不希望我给你带来这样的不幸。”

When the dancing recommenced, however, and Darcy approached to claim her hand, Charlotte could not help cautioning her, in a whisper, not to be a simpleton, and allow her fancy for Wickham to make her appear unpleasant in the eyes of a man often times his consequence.
跳舞重新开始时，查理特不得不小声警告她，不要做一个傻瓜，不要让自己的想象让自己的形象在男人面前显得不那么讨人喜欢。

Elizabeth made no answer, and took her place in the set, amazed at the dignity to which she was arrived in being allowed to stand opposite to Mr. Darcy, and reading in her neighbours’ looks their equal amazement in beholding it.
詹姆斯没有回答，她坐下来，惊讶于自己已经到达了能够站在达西先生对面的尊严，并且读着邻居们脸上同样的惊讶，他们看着她，看着她，看着她。

They stood for some time without speaking a word; and she began to imagine that their silence was to last through the two dances, and, at first, was resolved not to break it; till suddenly fancying that it would be the greater punishment to her partner to oblige him to talk, she made some slight observation on the dance.
他们站了一会儿没有说话，她开始想象他们的沉默会持续到两个舞会结束，她决定不打破沉默，直到突然想象到让她的舞伴说话会给她带来更大的惩罚，她做出了一个关于舞蹈的轻微观察。
He replied, and was again silent.
他回答了，再次沉默。
After a pause of some minutes, she addressed him a second time, with—
他们沉默了一会儿，她第二次对他说道——
“It is your turn to say something now, Mr. Darcy.
“轮到你说了，达西先生。
I talked about the dance, and you ought to make some kind of remark on the size of the room, or the number of couples.”
我谈了关于舞蹈，你应该说一些关于房间大小或者舞伴数量的话。”
He smiled, and assured her that whatever she wished him to say should be said.
他微笑，保证她，无论她希望他说什么，他都会说。
“Very well; that reply will do for the present.
“很好，这个回答现在就足够了。
Perhaps, by-and-by, I may observe that private balls are much pleasanter than public ones; but now we may be silent.”
可能，以后我可能会注意到私人舞会比公共舞会更愉快，但现在我们可以保持沉默。”
“Do you talk by rule, then, while you are dancing?”
你说话是有规矩的，跳舞时吗？
“Sometimes.
有时。
One must speak a little, you know.
说话是必要的。

It would look odd to be entirely silent for half an hour together; and yet, for the advantage of some, conversation ought to be so arranged as that they may have the trouble of saying as little as possible.”
交谈应当安排得让对方尽量少说。
“Are you consulting your own feelings in the present case, or do you imagine that you are gratifying mine?”
你是在考虑自己的感受，还是认为是在迎合我的感受？
“Both,” replied Elizabeth archly; “for I have always seen a great similarity in the turn of our minds.
“都”，丽莎回道，“因为我总看到我们俩的思维很相似。

We are each of an unsocial, taciturn disposition, unwilling to speak, unless we expect to say something that will amaze the whole room, and be handed down to posterity with all the éclat of a proverb.”
我们俩都是不善言辞、沉默寡言的人，不愿说话，除非我们期望说出一些能震惊全场的话，并且被传为佳话。
“This is no very striking resemblance of your own character, I am sure,” said he.
“这和你自己的性格很相似，我敢肯定。”他说。
“How near it may be to mine, I cannot pretend to say.
“我不能说它和我的很相似，我不能假装说。
You think it a faithful portrait, undoubtedly.”
你认为它是一幅忠实的画像。
“I must not decide on my own performance.”
“我不能决定自己的表现。”
He made no answer; and they were again silent till they had gone down the dance, when he asked her if she and her sisters did not very often walk to Meryton.
他没有回答，他们又沉默了，直到他们下舞池，他问她和她的姐妹们是否经常去米尔登镇散步。
She answered in the affirmative; and, unable to resist the temptation, added, “When you met us there the other day, we had just been forming a new acquaintance.”
她回答是的，他无法抗拒诱惑，补充道，“当我们上次在那儿遇到我们的时候，我们刚刚结识了。”
The effect was immediate.
效果立竿见影。
A deeper shade of hauteur overspread his features, but he said not a word; and Elizabeth, though blaming herself for her own weakness, could not go on.
他脸上露出更深的傲慢，但没有说一句话，而丽莎虽然责备自己，但无法继续。
At length Darcy spoke, and in a constrained manner said,—
最后，达西开口说话，用一种勉强的语气说——
“Mr. Wickham is blessed with such happy manners as may insure his making friends; whether he may be equally capable of retaining them, is less certain.”
“威克姆先生拥有如此幸福的举止，可以确保他交到朋友；至于他是否能够保持这些朋友，就不太确定了。”
“He has been so unlucky as to lose your friendship,” replied Elizabeth, with emphasis, “and in a manner which he is likely to suffer from all his life.”
“他不幸失去了你的友谊，”丽莎强调说，“而且这种失去是会伴随他一生的。”
Darcy made no answer, and seemed desirous of changing the subject.
达西没有回答，似乎想要改变话题。

At that moment Sir William Lucas appeared close to them, meaning to pass through the set to the other side of the room; but, on perceiving Mr. Darcy, he stopped, with a bow of superior courtesy, to compliment him on his dancing and his partner.
正当这时，威廉·卢卡斯出现在他们身边，准备穿过围栏到房间的另一边；但一看到达西，他停下脚步，向他致以尊敬的礼节，称赞他跳舞和舞伴。
“I have been most highly gratified, indeed, my dear sir; such very superior dancing is not often seen.
“我非常高兴，亲爱的先生；如此优秀的舞蹈，很少见到。”
It is evident that you belong to the first circles.
显然，你属于上层圈子。

Allow me to say, however, that your fair partner does not disgrace you: and that I must hope to have this pleasure often repeated, especially when a certain desirable event, my dear Miss Eliza (glancing at her sister and Bingley), shall take place.
允许我告诉你，你的漂亮舞伴并不让你丢脸：我希望这种快乐能够经常重复，特别是在某个值得期待的事件发生时，我的亲爱的小姐（瞥了一眼姐姐和宾利）。
What congratulations will then flow in!
那些祝贺将随之而来！
I appeal to Mr. Darcy;—but let me not interrupt you, sir.
我向达西先生请教；但让我不要打断你，先生。
You will not thank me for detaining you from the bewitching converse of that young lady, whose bright eyes are also upbraiding me.”
你不会感谢我打断你与那位年轻小姐的迷人交谈，她明亮的眼睛也在责备我。

The latter part of this address was scarcely heard by Darcy; but Sir William’s allusion to his friend seemed to strike him forcibly, and his eyes were directed, with a very serious expression, towards Bingley and Jane, who were dancing together.
这段话的后半部分，达西几乎听不到，但威廉·卢卡斯提到他的朋友似乎让他印象深刻，他的眼睛带着非常严肃的表情，转向正在跳舞的宾利和简，他们正在一起跳舞。
Recovering himself, however, shortly, he turned to his partner, and said,—
他恢复了自己，不久后，他转向他的舞伴，说——
“Sir William’s interruption has made me forget what we were talking of.”
“威廉·卢卡斯的打断使我忘记了我们正在谈论什么。”
“I do not think we were speaking at all.
“我不认为我们正在谈论什么。
Sir William could not have interrupted any two people in the room who had less to say for themselves.
威廉大人在房间里，除了两人，没有比他们更少要说的。
We have tried two or three subjects already without success, and what we are to talk of next I cannot imagine.”
我们已经试了两次或三次，都没有成功，我想象不出接下来要谈什么。
“What think you of books?” said he, smiling.
“你对书有什么看法？”他笑着说。
“Books—oh no!—I am sure we never read the same, or not with the same feelings.”
“书——哦，不！——我肯定我们从不读同样的书，或者没有同样的感受。
“I am sorry you think so; but if that be the case, there can at least be no want of subject.
“我很抱歉，但如果你认为这样，那么至少就不会缺少话题。
We may compare our different opinions.”
我们可以比较我们的不同看法。
“No—I cannot talk of books in a ball-room; my head is always full of something else.”
“不——我不在舞会上谈论书。我的头总是满是其他事情。
“The present always occupies you in such scenes—does it?” said he, with a look of doubt.
“现在总是在你身上占据着你——是吗？”他说，带着怀疑的目光。

“Yes, always,” she replied, without knowing what she said; for her thoughts had wandered far from the subject, as soon afterwards appeared by her suddenly exclaiming, “I remember hearing you once say, Mr. Darcy, that you hardly ever forgave;—that your resentment, once created, was unappeasable.
“是的，总是。”她回答，不知道自己说了什么，因为她的思绪已经远远偏离了这个话题，后来突然叫道：“我记得曾经听你说过，达西先生，你很少原谅，——你对怨恨的产生，从来没有被平息。
You are very cautious, I suppose, as to its being created?”
你很小心，我想，关于它的产生？”
“I am,” said he, with a firm voice.
“我”，他说，声音坚定。
“And never allow yourself to be blinded by prejudice?”
“并且从不被偏见所蒙蔽？”
“I hope not.”
“我希望没有。”
“It is particularly incumbent on those who never change their opinion, to be secure of judging properly at first.”
“那些从不改变自己观点的人，尤其应该注意，要能正确地判断最初。”
“May I ask to what these questions tend?”
“我可以问这些问题有什么目的？”
“Merely to the illustration of your character,” said she, endeavouring to shake off her gravity.
“仅仅为了说明你的性格，”她试图摆脱自己的严肃。
“I am trying to make it out.”
“我正在努力理解。”
“And what is your success?”
“你的成功如何？”
She shook her head.
她摇了摇头。
“I do not get on at all.
“我一点也不适应。
I hear such different accounts of you as puzzle me exceedingly.”
我听说关于你的情况有如此不同的说法，让我感到非常困惑。”

“I can readily believe,” answered he, gravely, “that reports may vary greatly with respect to me; and I could wish, Miss Bennet, that you were not to sketch my character at the present moment, as there is reason to fear that the performance would reflect no credit on either.”
“我完全相信，”他冷淡地回答，“关于我的报告可能会有很大的差异；我希望，简·班nett小姐，你现在不要画出我的性格，因为有理由担心，这样的表演不会对我或你有任何不尊重。”
“But if I do not take your likeness now, I may never have another opportunity.”
“但是如果我现在不画出你的肖像，我可能永远没有另一个机会。”
“I would by no means suspend any pleasure of yours,” he coldly replied.
“我不会因为任何对你的好处而暂停的，”他冷淡地回答。

She said no more, and they went down the other dance and parted in silence; on each side dissatisfied, though not to an equal degree; for in Darcy’s breast there was a tolerably powerful feeling towards her, which soon procured her pardon, and directed all his anger against another.
她没有再多说什么，他们一起走下另一场舞会，沉默地分开；在他们各自的一边都不满意，尽管程度不完全相同；因为在我德纳第的心中，对她的有一份相当强烈的感觉，不久就得到了她的原谅，并且将所有的愤怒都指向了另一个。
They had not long separated when Miss Bingley came towards her, and, with an expression of civil disdain, thus accosted her,—
他们没有长时间分开，当简·班nett小姐走近她时，她带着一种鄙视的神情这样对她说道——
“So, Miss Eliza, I hear you are quite delighted with George Wickham?
“所以，简·伊丽莎，听说你对乔治·韦克汉姆非常高兴？

Your sister has been talking to me about him, and asking me a thousand questions; and I find that the young man forgot to tell you, among his other communications, that he was the son of old Wickham, the late Mr. Darcy’s steward.
你的姐姐一直在和我谈论他，并问我许多问题；我发现这个年轻人忘记告诉过你，除了其他通信之外，他还提到他父亲是老韦克汉姆，老韦克汉姆是前先生·达西的管家。

Let me recommend you, however, as a friend, not to give implicit confidence to all his assertions; for, as to Mr. Darcy’s using him ill, it is perfectly false: for, on the contrary, he has been always remarkably kind to him, though George Wickham has treated Mr. Darcy in a most infamous manner.
但是，让我推荐你作为朋友，不要完全相信他所有的说法；因为关于先生·达西的他很坏，完全错误：相反，他一直非常善良地对待他，尽管乔治·韦克汉姆对先生·达西非常不友好。

I do not know the particulars, but I know very well that Mr. Darcy is not in the least to blame; that he cannot bear to hear George Wickham mentioned; and that though my brother thought he could not well avoid including him in his invitation to the officers, he was excessively glad to find that he had taken himself out of the way.
我不知道详情，但我知道很清楚，先生·达西一点也不错；他不能忍受听到乔治·韦克汉姆的名字；相反，他一直非常善良地对待他，尽管乔治·韦克汉姆对先生·达西非常不友好。
His coming into the country at all is a most insolent thing, indeed, and I wonder how he could presume to do it.
他的到来简直是一种傲慢无礼的行为，我真怀疑他有什么资格这么做。
I pity you, Miss Eliza, for this discovery of your favourite’s guilt; but really, considering his descent, one could not expect much better.”
我可怜你，珍小姐，因为发现你最喜爱的人的罪行；但是，真的，考虑到他的出身，我们不能期望更多。

“His guilt and his descent appear, by your account, to be the same,” said Elizabeth, angrily; “for I have heard you accuse him of nothing worse than of being the son of Mr. Darcy’s steward, and of that, I can assure you, he informed me himself.”
“他的罪行和他的出身看起来是一样的，”伊丽莎白生气地说，“因为我听说你指控他除了是达西先生管家的儿子之外，什么罪行都没有。”
“I beg your pardon,” replied Miss Bingley, turning away with a sneer.
“对不起，”宾利小姐回答，带着冷笑。
“Excuse my interference; it was kindly meant.”
“对不起我的插手，这是出于善意。”
“Insolent girl!” said Elizabeth to herself.
“傲慢的小女孩！”伊丽莎白对自己说。
“You are much mistaken if you expect to influence me by such a paltry attack as this.
“你对我的攻击太小看了，”说， “你期待通过这样的小插曲对我产生影响。”
I see nothing in it but your own wilful ignorance and the malice of Mr. Darcy.”
我看不出这有什么，只是你自己的无知和达西先生的恶意。
She then sought her eldest sister, who had undertaken to make inquiries on the same subject of Bingley.
她随后去找了姐姐，她已经承担起调查与宾利有关的事情。
Jane met her with a smile of such sweet complacency, a glow of such happy expression, as sufficiently marked how well she was satisfied with the occurrences of the evening.
约翰逊小姐微笑着，对这种晚上的发生的事情感到满意，脸上洋溢着幸福的表情。

Elizabeth instantly read her feelings; and, at that moment, solicitude for Wickham, resentment against his enemies, and everything else, gave way before the hope of Jane’s being in the fairest way for happiness.
伊丽莎白立刻读出了她的感情，此时，对威克汉姆的担忧、对他的敌人怀恨在心，以及一切其他东西，都让位于对约翰的幸福的希望。
“I want to know,” said she, with a countenance no less smiling than her sister’s, “what you have learnt about Mr. Wickham.
“我想知道，”她用比姐姐更微笑的面孔说，“你对威克汉姆了解些什么？”
But perhaps you have been too pleasantly engaged to think of any third person, in which case you may be sure of my pardon.”
但是也许你太愉快了，以至于没有想起第三个，那么你就可以宽恕我了。
“No,” replied Jane, “I have not forgotten him; but I have nothing satisfactory to tell you.
“不，”简说，“我没有忘记他；但是我没有什么可以告诉你的东西。

Mr. Bingley does not know the whole of his history, and is quite ignorant of the circumstances which have principally offended Mr. Darcy; but he will vouch for the good conduct, the probity and honour, of his friend, and is perfectly convinced that Mr. Wickham has deserved much less attention from Mr. Darcy than he has received; and I am sorry to say that by his account, as well as his sister’s, Mr. Wickham is by no means a respectable young man.
宾利先生不知道他的全部历史，对达西先生所冒犯的细节一无所知；但是他会担保他的朋友的品行、正直和荣誉，而且完全相信威克汉姆先生受到了比他所收到的更多的关注；而且我不得不说，根据他的说法，以及他的姐姐的说法，威克汉姆先生不是一个体面的年轻人。
I am afraid he has been very imprudent, and has deserved to lose Mr. Darcy’s regard.”
我很担心他过于鲁莽，理应失去达西先生的青睐。
“Mr. Bingley does not know Mr. Wickham himself.”
“布莱克尼先生并不认识威克姆先生本人。”
“No; he never saw him till the other morning at Meryton.”
“不，他直到前天在米尔登顿才见到他。”
“This account then is what he has received from Mr. Darcy.
“这份报告是根据达西先生收到的。”
I am perfectly satisfied.
我完全放心。
But what does he say of the living?”
但是他说什么关于活的呢？
“He does not exactly recollect the circumstances, though he has heard them from Mr. Darcy more than once, but he believes that it was left to him conditionally only.”
“他并不确切记得那些情况，虽然他从达西先生那里听了很多次，但他相信是留给他的条件。”
“I have not a doubt of Mr. Bingley’s sincerity,” said Elizabeth warmly, “but you must excuse my not being convinced by assurances only.
“我对布莱克尼先生的真诚很有信心，”丽兹热情地说，“但你必须原谅我只听信保证。”

Mr. Bingley’s defence of his friend was a very able one, I dare say; but since he is unacquainted with several parts of the story, and has learnt the rest from that friend himself, I shall venture still to think of both gentlemen as I did before.”
布莱克尼先生对朋友的辩护非常有力，我敢说；但既然他不熟悉故事的某些部分，又从那个朋友那里听到了这些，我仍然认为两个先生都像以前一样。
She then changed the discourse to one more gratifying to each, and on which there could be no difference of sentiment.
她然后把话题转向更令人满意的方面，并且在这个问题上没有分歧。
Elizabeth listened with delight to the happy though modest hopes which Jane entertained of Bingley’s regard, and said all in her power to heighten her confidence in it.
伊丽莎白对简对布莱克尼先生的爱慕的幸福而谦逊的希望感到高兴，并竭力提高她的信心。

On their being joined by Mr. Bingley himself, Elizabeth withdrew to Miss Lucas; to whose inquiry after the pleasantness of her last partner she had scarcely replied, before Mr. Collins came up to them, and told her with great exultation, that he had just been so fortunate as to make a most important discovery.
当他们被布莱克尼先生本人接见时，伊丽莎白到卢卡斯小姐那里去了。她对简关于她最后的伙伴的询问几乎没有回答，就在马修·康塞尔上来告诉他们他刚刚很幸运地发现了一件重要的事情时，她就回答了。
“I have found out,” said he, “by a singular accident, that there is now in the room a near relation to my patroness.
他说：“我查出了，”“ ”靠一个奇特的偶然，“我发现现在房间里有一个我的主子的近亲。”
I happened to overhear the gentleman himself mentioning to the young lady who does the honours of this house the names of his cousin Miss De Bourgh, and of her mother, Lady Catherine.
我恰好听到那位绅士本人在提到接待这家人家的年轻 lady 的名字时提到了他表亲黛博赫小姐和她的母亲卡瑟琳夫人。
How wonderfully these sort of things occur!
多么奇妙的事情！
Who would have thought of my meeting with—perhaps—a nephew of Lady Catherine de Bourgh in this assembly!
也许，我遇到了——或许——柯林斯伯爵夫人的一个侄儿。
I am most thankful that the discovery is made in time for me to pay my respects to him, which I am now going to do, and trust he will excuse my not having done it before.
我非常感谢这个发现，正好让我有时间向他表示敬意，现在我将这样做，并希望他能原谅我之前没有这样做。
My total ignorance of the connection must plead my apology.”
我对这种关系一无所知，必须为我的道歉。
“You are not going to introduce yourself to Mr. Darcy?”
“你不会介绍自己给达西先生吧？”
“Indeed I am.
“当然。”
I shall entreat his pardon for not having done it earlier.
我会向他道歉，因为我没有在之前这样做。
I believe him to be Lady Catherine’s nephew.
我认为他是柯林斯伯爵夫人的侄儿。
It will be in my power to assure him that her Ladyship was quite well yesterday se’nnight.”
我有能力向他保证，昨天晚上柯林斯夫人非常健康。

Elizabeth tried hard to dissuade him from such a scheme; assuring him that Mr. Darcy would consider his addressing him without introduction as an impertinent freedom, rather than a compliment to his aunt; that it was not in the least necessary there should be any notice on either side, and that if it were, it must belong to Mr. Darcy, the superior in consequence, to begin the acquaintance.
Elizabeth 努力劝阻他实施这样的计划；告诉他达西先生会认为没有介绍就称呼他为一种傲慢，而不是对他的姑妈的一种敬意；这并不是双方都需要有任何表示，如果需要的话，那也只能是达西先生，地位较高的人，先开始结识。
Mr. Collins listened to her with the determined air of following his own inclination, and when she ceased speaking, replied thus,—
Mr. Collins 听了她的话，带着坚定的语气，当她停止说话时，回答道：

“My dear Miss Elizabeth, I have the highest opinion in the world of your excellent judgment in all matters within the scope of your understanding, but permit me to say that there must be a wide difference between the established forms of ceremony amongst the laity and those which regulate the clergy; for, give me leave to observe that I consider the clerical office as equal in point of dignity with the highest rank in the kingdom—provided that a proper humility of behaviour is at the same time maintained.
亲爱的伊丽莎白小姐，我对你在理解范围内的所有事务中卓越判断的最高评价是世界上最高的，但是请允许我说，世俗和宗教中的礼仪形式之间一定存在很大的差异；因为，让我冒昧地说，我认为牧师的职位与王国中的最高爵位一样尊贵——前提是同时保持适当的行为谦卑。
You must, therefore, allow me to follow the dictates of my conscience on this occasion, which lead me to perform what I look on as a point of duty.
因此，你必须允许我根据我的良心行事，这使我必须执行我看来是义务的事情。

Pardon me for neglecting to profit by your advice, which on every other subject shall be my constant guide, though in the case before us I consider myself more fitted by education and habitual study to decide on what is right than a young lady like yourself;” and with a low bow he left her to attack Mr. Darcy, whose reception of his advances she eagerly watched, and whose astonishment at being so addressed was very evident.
对不起我忽视了你的建议，这在其他方面将是我始终的指南，但在我们面前，我认为自己比像你这样的年轻女士更适合决定什么是对的；”并低着头离开了她，去攻击达西先生，她非常期待他的回应，他被这样对待的惊讶非常明显。

Her cousin prefaced his speech with a solemn bow, and though she could not hear a word of it, she felt as if hearing it all, and saw in the motion of his lips the words “apology,” “Hunsford,” and “Lady Catherine de Bourgh.”
她的表亲在发言前做了庄严的鞠躬，尽管她听不到他说的话，她感觉好像听到了所有的话，她看到嘴唇的动作是“道歉”，“Hunsford”，和“柯林斯伯爵夫人”。
It vexed her to see him expose himself to such a man.
见他这样暴露自己，她很生气。
Mr. Darcy was eyeing him with unrestrained wonder; and when at last Mr. Collins allowed him to speak, replied with an air of distant civility.
我斯·达西的目光不住地停留在他身上，他那无法抑制的惊奇之情溢于言表。当斯·柯林斯允许他发言时，他以一种遥远的礼貌回应道。

Mr. Collins, however, was not discouraged from speaking again, and Mr. Darcy’s contempt seemed abundantly increasing with the length of his second speech; and at the end of it he only made him a slight bow, and moved another way: Mr. Collins then returned to Elizabeth.
斯·柯林斯再次发言时，他并未因此而灰心，斯·达西的轻蔑似乎随着他第二段话的冗长而愈发强烈。在最后，他只是对他微微行了个礼，然后转身走了。斯·柯林斯随后又回到了伊丽莎白身边。
“I have no reason, I assure you,” said he, “to be dissatisfied with my reception.
“我保证，”他说，“我没有任何理由感到不满足。”
Mr. Darcy seemed much pleased with the attention.
斯·达西似乎对她的关注感到非常高兴。

He answered me with the utmost civility, and even paid me the compliment of saying, that he was so well convinced of Lady Catherine’s discernment as to be certain she could never bestow a favour unworthily.
他以最礼貌的回应，甚至对我表示了敬意，说我确信，尽管她母亲对她的看法，她肯定不会将一个不值得的恩惠给予她。
It was really a very handsome thought.
这真是一个非常美好的想法。
Upon the whole, I am much pleased with him.”
总体来说，我对他很满意。

As Elizabeth had no longer any interest of her own to pursue, she turned her attention almost entirely on her sister and Mr. Bingley; and the train of agreeable reflections which her observations gave birth to made her perhaps almost as happy as Jane.
伊丽莎白已经没有了任何自己追求的动机，她几乎完全关注着她的姐姐和斯·比奇利。她观察到的这些评论使她可能几乎和简一样幸福。

She saw her in idea settled in that very house, in all the felicity which a marriage of true affection could bestow; and she felt capable, under such circumstances, of endeavouring even to like Bingley’s two sisters.
她看到在她想象中，她和她姐姐和斯·比奇利都住在一个地方，享受着真挚的爱所带来的幸福；她觉得自己在这样的情况下，甚至能够尽力去喜欢比奇利的两个姐妹。
Her mother’s thoughts she plainly saw were bent the same way, and she determined not to venture near her, lest she might hear too much.
她母亲的想法，她明显看得出来，都是一样的，她决定不要接近她，以免听到太多。

When they sat down to supper, therefore, she considered it a most unlucky perverseness which placed them within one of each other; and deeply was she vexed to find that her mother was talking to that one person (Lady Lucas) freely, openly, and of nothing else but of her expectation that Jane would be soon married to Mr. Bingley.
因为他们坐下来吃饭，所以她认为这是一个非常不幸的偏见，将他们放在彼此的旁边，她深深地感到，她母亲正在自由地谈论那个一个人（卢卡斯夫人），谈论她对简很快结婚到斯·比奇利的期望。
It was an animating subject, and Mrs. Bennet seemed incapable of fatigue while enumerating the advantages of the match.
这是一个鼓舞人心的话题，母亲似乎无法疲劳，当她列举这个婚姻的好处时。

His being such a charming young man, and so rich, and living but three miles from them, were the first points of self-gratulation; and then it was such a comfort to think how fond the two sisters were of Jane, and to be certain that they must desire the connection as much as she could do.
他的魅力，他如此富有，他住在他们三英里之外，都是他第一个自我满足的点；然后，想到两个姐妹如此热爱简，他确信，她们肯定会像她一样，想要这种联系。

It was, moreover, such a promising thing for her younger daughters, as Jane’s marrying so greatly must throw them in the way of other rich men; and, lastly, it was so pleasant at her time of life to be able to consign her single daughters to the care of their sister, that she might not be obliged to go into company more than she liked.
除此之外，这对她年幼的女儿来说，是一个非常有希望的事情，因为简的婚姻，这将使她们有机会遇到其他富有的人；最后，她觉得在她年纪的时候，能够把她的单女儿交给她们的姐姐，她可能不必去公司，她喜欢的。

It was necessary to make this circumstance a matter of pleasure, because on such occasions it is the etiquette; but no one was less likely than Mrs. Bennet to find comfort in staying at home at any period of her life.
因为在这样的场合，这是礼仪，但没有人比斯·班纳特更不可能在她一生中的任何时期找到在家的安慰。
She concluded with many good wishes that Lady Lucas might soon be equally fortunate, though evidently and triumphantly believing there was no chance of it.
她最后满怀好意地祝愿路易丝夫人能很快幸运起来，尽管她显然坚信自己不可能幸运。

In vain did Elizabeth endeavour to check the rapidity of her mother’s words, or persuade her to describe her felicity in a less audible whisper; for to her inexpressible vexation she could perceive that the chief of it was overheard by Mr. Darcy, who sat opposite to them.
莉莉丝努力想阻止母亲滔滔不绝的说话，或者说服她用更低的声音描述自己的幸福，但令她无比恼火的是，她发现那位大名鼎鼎的达西先生正坐在他们对面，听到了她的谈话。
Her mother only scolded her for being nonsensical.
她母亲只责骂她胡言乱语。
“What is Mr. Darcy to me, pray, that I should be afraid of him?
“什么，亲爱的，我怕他吗？”
I am sure we owe him no such particular civility as to be obliged to say nothing he may not like to hear.”
我敢肯定，我们欠他一点特别的礼貌，不要说他不喜欢听的话。”
“For heaven’s sake, madam, speak lower.
“亲爱的，说话要低一点。”
What advantage can it be to you to offend Mr. Darcy?
有什么好处是你去冒犯达西先生？
You will never recommend yourself to his friend by so doing.”
你不会通过这样做来推荐自己给他的朋友。
Nothing that she could say, however, had any influence.
她说的任何话都没有影响。
Her mother would talk of her views in the same intelligible tone.
她母亲会用同样的清晰的语调谈论她的观点。
Elizabeth blushed and blushed again with shame and vexation.
莉莉丝羞愧地红了脸，又羞又恼。

She could not help frequently glancing her eye at Mr. Darcy, though every glance convinced her of what she dreaded; for though he was not always looking at her mother, she was convinced that his attention was invariably fixed by her.
她忍不住多次偷偷地用眼睛瞟向达西先生，尽管每一次瞟都让她更加害怕，因为尽管他不总是看着她母亲，但她确定他的注意力总是固定在她身上。
The expression of his face changed gradually from indignant contempt to a composed and steady gravity.
他的脸上表情逐渐从愤怒的轻蔑到一种冷静而坚定的严肃。

At length, however, Mrs. Bennet had no more to say; and Lady Lucas, who had been long yawning at the repetition of delights which she saw no likelihood of sharing, was left to the comforts of cold ham and chicken.
最后，不过，贝恩斯夫人不再说什么了，而路易丝夫人，看到她看到的那些不可能分享的快乐，已经长时间打哈欠，被留下享受冷香肠和鸡肉的安慰。
Elizabeth now began to revive.
莉莉丝现在开始恢复了。

But not long was the interval of tranquillity; for when supper was over, singing was talked of, and she had the mortification of seeing Mary, after very little entreaty, preparing to oblige the company.
但没过多久，宁静就结束了。因为晚餐过后，有人提议唱歌，她不得不忍受看到玛丽在几乎没有请求的情况下准备表演的尴尬。

By many significant looks and silent entreaties did she endeavour to prevent such a proof of complaisance,—but in vain; Mary would not understand them; such an opportunity of exhibiting was delightful to her, and she began her song.
通过许多意味深长的眼神和无声的恳求，她试图阻止这样的证明——但徒劳无功；玛丽不明白这些眼神，这样的机会对她来说非常愉快，她开始唱歌。

Elizabeth’s eyes were fixed on her, with most painful sensations; and she watched her progress through the several stanzas with an impatience which was very ill rewarded at their close; for Mary, on receiving amongst the thanks of the table the hint of a hope that she might be prevailed on to favour them again, after the pause of half a minute began another.
伊丽莎白的眼睛里充满了最痛苦的感受，她注视着她的进展，每一节诗都怀着非常难以满足的 impatient，因为在诗结束时，玛丽在餐桌上的感谢中收到希望她可能被说服再次为他们表演的提示后，经过半分钟的暂停，便开始另一首诗。
Mary’s powers were by no means fitted for such a display; her voice was weak, and her manner affected.
玛丽的才能并不适合这样的展示；她的声音是虚弱的，她的态度是受影响的。
Elizabeth was in agonies.
伊丽莎白在痛不欲生之中。
She looked at Jane to see how she bore it; but Jane was very composedly talking to Bingley.
她看着简，想知道她如何忍受；但简非常镇定地和宾利交谈。
She looked at his two sisters, and saw them making signs of derision at each other, and at Darcy, who continued, however, impenetrably grave.
她看着他的两个姐妹，看到她们彼此嘲笑，甚至嘲笑达西，尽管他继续保持着不可穿透的严肃。
She looked at her father to entreat his interference, lest Mary should be singing all night.
她看着她的父亲，恳求他的干涉，以免玛丽在晚上一直唱歌。
He took the hint, and, when Mary had finished her second song, said aloud,—
他抓住这个暗示，当玛丽在唱完第二首后，大声说：
“That will do extremely well, child.
“那太好了，孩子。
You have delighted us long enough.
你已经让我们唱得太久了。
Let the other young ladies have time to exhibit.”
让其他年轻小姐有时间展示。”
Mary, though pretending not to hear, was somewhat disconcerted; and Elizabeth, sorry for her, and sorry for her father’s speech, was afraid her anxiety had done no good.
玛丽虽然假装没听见，但有些不安；而爱莎为她担心，也为她父亲的言论感到抱歉，她害怕自己的焦虑没有起到好的效果。
Others of the party were now applied to.
其他人现在被应用了。

“If I,” said Mr. Collins, “were so fortunate as to be able to sing, I should have great pleasure, I am sure, in obliging the company with an air; for I consider music as a very innocent diversion, and perfectly compatible with the profession of a clergyman.
“如果我，”说克林顿先生，“有幸能唱歌，我肯定会很高兴，我相信，能为公司带来一首曲子；因为我认为音乐是一种非常无辜的消遣，完全适合牧师的职业。”
I do not mean, however, to assert that we can be justified in devoting too much of our time to music, for there are certainly other things to be attended to.
我的意思并不是说我们应当把太多的时间浪费在音乐上，因为确实还有其他事情需要处理。
The rector of a parish has much to do.
一个教区的主教有很多事情要做。
In the first place, he must make such an agreement for tithes as may be beneficial to himself and not offensive to his patron.
首先，他必须与教区主教达成一个有利于他自己而不冒犯到他的资助人的协议。

He must write his own sermons; and the time that remains will not be too much for his parish duties, and the care and improvement of his dwelling, which he cannot be excused from making as comfortable as possible.
他必须自己写自己的讲道，剩下的时间不会太多用于他的教区职责，以及他无法推卸的责任和改善住所的护理，这可以尽可能舒适。
And I do not think it of light importance that he should have attentive and conciliatory manners towards everybody, especially towards those to whom he owes his preferment.
我认为他必须对任何人，尤其是对那些使他升迁的人表现出关注和和气的态度。
I cannot acquit him of that duty; nor could I think well of the man who should omit an occasion of testifying his respect towards anybody connected with the family.”
我不能原谅他，我也认为一个不表现对任何与家庭有关的人表示尊重的人是不好的。
And with a bow to Mr. Darcy, he concluded his speech, which had been spoken so loud as to be heard by half the room.
他向德纳第先生鞠了一躬，结束了他的演讲，这演讲的声音太大，以至于整个房间的人都听到了。

Many stared—many smiled; but no one looked more amused than Mr. Bennet himself, while his wife seriously commended Mr. Collins for having spoken so sensibly, and observed, in a half-whisper to Lady Lucas, that he was a remarkably clever, good kind of young man.
许多人注视着——许多人微笑；但没有人比伊丽莎白的丈夫更感到愉快，而他的妻子则严肃地称赞了查尔斯·康沃尔先生，认为他说话很明智，并且在半低语中对卢卡斯夫人说，他是一个非常聪明，善良的小伙子。

To Elizabeth it appeared, that had her family made an agreement to expose themselves as much as they could during the evening, it would have been impossible for them to play their parts with more spirit, or finer success; and happy did she think it for Bingley and her sister that some of the exhibition had escaped his notice, and that his feelings were not of a sort to be much distressed by the folly which he must have witnessed.
对于伊丽莎白来说，看起来如果她的家庭在晚上暴露自己尽可能多，他们将无法以更精神或更成功的表演来表演他们的角色；她认为对于比内利和她姐姐来说，有些表演逃脱了他的注意，以及他的感觉不会因为他在看到这个愚蠢的行为而受到很大影响。

That his two sisters and Mr. Darcy, however, should have such an opportunity of ridiculing her relations was bad enough; and she could not determine whether the silent contempt of the gentleman, or the insolent smiles of the ladies, were more intolerable.
但是，她不能确定，她姐姐和查尔斯·达西，以及她的家人，是否有机会嘲笑她的亲戚是不好的；她不能确定，沉默的蔑视，或者女士们傲慢的微笑，哪一个更难以忍受。
The rest of the evening brought her little amusement.
这个晚上剩下的时间带来了一些小的娱乐。
She was teased by Mr. Collins, who continued most perseveringly by her side; and though he could not prevail with her to dance with him again, put it out of her power to dance with others.
伊丽莎白被查尔斯·康沃尔先生持续地纠缠在身边，尽管他不能迫使她再次与他跳舞，但阻止她与其他人跳舞。
In vain did she entreat him to stand up with somebody else, and offered to introduce him to any young lady in the room.
他恳求他站起来和某个人，然后提出把他们介绍给房间里的任何一个年轻女士。

He assured her that, as to dancing, he was perfectly indifferent to it; that his chief object was, by delicate attentions, to recommend himself to her; and that he should therefore make a point of remaining close to her the whole evening.
他保证她跳舞对他完全不重要，他主要的目标是通过微妙的注意来推荐自己给她，因此他将尽一切努力保持与她在一起。
There was no arguing upon such a project.
对于这样的项目，没有争论。
She owed her greatest relief to her friend Miss Lucas, who often joined them, and good-naturedly engaged Mr. Collins’s conversation to herself.
她最大的解脱来自她的朋友路易丝小姐，她经常加入他们，而且善良地把查尔斯先生的谈话转到自己身上。
She was at least free from the offence of Mr. Darcy’s further notice: though often standing within a very short distance of her, quite disengaged, he never came near enough to speak.
她至少免除了对查尔斯先生进一步注意的罪行：尽管他经常离她很近，却完全脱离了视线，他从不接近到能说话的程度。
She felt it to be the probable consequence of her allusions to Mr. Wickham, and rejoiced in it.
她觉得这是她对查尔斯先生的暗示所导致的可能后果，并因此感到高兴。

The Longbourn party were the last of all the company to depart; and by a manœuvre of Mrs. Bennet had to wait for their carriage a quarter of an hour after everybody else was gone, which gave them time to see how heartily they were wished away by some of the family.
长门堡庄园的客人是最后离开的，而由贝恩斯太太的巧妙安排，他们不得不等到其他人离开后才离开，这给了他们时间看到家人是如何热烈地告别他们的。
Mrs. Hurst and her sister scarcely opened their mouths except to complain of fatigue, and were evidently impatient to have the house to themselves.
贝恩斯太太和她的妹妹几乎不开口，除了抱怨疲劳，显然急于独自拥有房子。

They repulsed every attempt of Mrs. Bennet at conversation, and, by so doing, threw a languor over the whole party, which was very little relieved by the long speeches of Mr. Collins, who was complimenting Mr. Bingley and his sisters on the elegance of their entertainment, and the hospitality and politeness which had marked their behaviour to their guests.
他们拒绝了贝恩斯太太的交谈，通过这种方式，整个聚会笼罩了一种倦怠感，这在查尔斯先生的长篇讲话中并没有得到缓解，他称赞宾利先生和他的姐妹们的优雅和招待客人时的礼貌和礼貌。
Darcy said nothing at all.
辛普森先生什么也没有说。
Mr. Bennet, in equal silence, was enjoying the scene.
贝恩斯先生在沉默中享受着这个场景。
Mr. Bingley and Jane were standing together a little detached from the rest, and talked only to each other.
宾利先生和简小姐站在一起，稍微远离其他人，只和对方交谈。

Elizabeth preserved as steady a silence as either Mrs. Hurst or Miss Bingley; and even Lydia was too much fatigued to utter more than the occasional exclamation of “Lord, how tired I am!” accompanied by a violent yawn.
莉迪亚保持了与贝恩斯太太和简小姐相同的沉默，甚至简小姐也因为疲惫而只能发出“天啊，我多么累啊！”的感叹，伴随着剧烈的打哈欠。

When at length they arose to take leave, Mrs. Bennet was most pressingly civil in her hope of seeing the whole family soon at Longbourn; and addressed herself particularly to Mr. Bingley, to assure him how happy he would make them, by eating a family dinner with them at any time, without the ceremony of a formal invitation.
当他们最后起身准备离开时，贝恩斯太太对看到整个家庭很快回到长门堡的希望非常殷切，并特意对宾利先生表示，他如何会让他们如此快乐，通过在他们回到伦敦后不久的任何时间里与他们共进家庭晚餐，而无需正式的邀请。

Bingley was all grateful pleasure; and he readily engaged for taking the earliest opportunity of waiting on her after his return from London, whither he was obliged to go the next day for a short time.
宾利先生非常感激，他很快同意了在返回伦敦后尽快等待他的机会，以便在宾利先生回来后不久拜访他们。

Mrs. Bennet was perfectly satisfied; and quitted the house under the delightful persuasion that, allowing for the necessary preparations of settlements, new carriages, and wedding clothes, she should undoubtedly see her daughter settled at Netherfield in the course of three or four months.
贝恩斯太太完全满意，她离开了房子，带着愉快的信念，尽管有必要的准备，如结算、新车、婚礼服装，她肯定会看到她的女儿在三个月内被安置在诺顿菲尔德。
Of having another daughter married to Mr. Collins she thought with equal certainty, and with considerable, though not equal, pleasure.
她对有另一个女儿嫁给宾利先生和诺顿菲尔德的匹配感到同样确定，尽管她对每个价值的评估都超过了宾利先生和诺顿菲尔德。
Elizabeth was the least dear to her of all her children; and though the man and the match were quite good enough for her, the worth of each was eclipsed by Mr. Bingley and Netherfield.
莉迪亚对她所有孩子中最亲近的她，以及她认为完全合适的男人和婚姻，她认为这与她对宾利先生和诺顿菲尔德的评价一样，尽管她对每个价值的评估都超过了宾利先生和诺顿菲尔德。
The next day opened a new scene at Longbourn.
第二天，长门庄园又上演了一幕新戏。
Mr. Collins made his declaration in form.
柯林斯先生按形式宣布了自己的意愿。

Having resolved to do it without loss of time, as his leave of absence extended only to the following Saturday, and having no feelings of diffidence to make it distressing to himself even at the moment, he set about it in a very orderly manner, with all the observances which he supposed a regular part of the business.
他决定不浪费时间，因为他休假只到下个星期六，而且没有自卑感让他在那一刻感到不安，他便按部就班地进行，按照他以为是正规商业程序的每一个细节。
On finding Mrs. Bennet, Elizabeth, and one of the younger girls together, soon after breakfast, he addressed the mother in these words,—
在早餐后不久，伊丽莎白和其中一个妹妹在一起时，他向母亲说这些话——
“May I hope, madam, for your interest with your fair daughter Elizabeth, when I solicit for the honour of a private audience with her in the course of this morning?”
“我希望能为您的女儿伊丽莎白的美貌和兴趣着想，当我在今天上午请求与她进行私人会面时，您是否愿意接受？”
Before Elizabeth had time for anything but a blush of surprise, Mrs. Bennet instantly answered,—
在伊丽莎白还没有来得及惊讶的时候，伯母就立刻回答了。
“Oh dear!
“哎呀，天啊！”
Yes, certainly.
当然，肯定的。
I am sure Lizzy will be very happy—I am sure she can have no objection.
我相信丽兹一定会非常高兴的——我相信她一定不会有任何异议的。
Come, Kitty, I want you upstairs.”
来吧，凯蒂，我想带你上去。
And gathering her work together, she was hastening away, when Elizabeth called out,—
她整理好工作，正要离开，伊丽莎白叫道——
“Dear ma’am, do not go.
“亲爱的夫人，请不要离开。”
I beg you will not go.
请不要离开。
Mr. Collins must excuse me.
柯林斯先生，请原谅我。
He can have nothing to say to me that anybody need not hear.
他的话对我来说，任何人不必听。
I am going away myself.”
我也要走了。
“No, no, nonsense, Lizzy.
“不，不，胡说八道，丽兹。
I desire you will stay where you are.”
我希望你能留在这里。”
And upon Elizabeth’s seeming really, with vexed and embarrassed looks, about to escape, she added, “Lizzy, I insist upon your staying and hearing Mr. Collins.”
女儿，我坚持你留在这里听听查尔斯先生的介绍。

Elizabeth would not oppose such an injunction; and a moment’s consideration making her also sensible that it would be wisest to get it over as soon and as quietly as possible, she sat down again, and tried to conceal, by incessant employment, the feelings which were divided between distress and diversion.
丽兹，我坚持你留在这里听听查尔斯先生的介绍。
Mrs. Bennet and Kitty walked off, and as soon as they were gone, Mr. Collins began,—
费恩伯恩太太和凯特走了，她们一走，查尔斯先生就开始了：
“Believe me, my dear Miss Elizabeth, that your modesty, so far from doing you any disservice, rather adds to your other perfections.
“相信我，亲爱的丽兹，你那小小的害羞反而增加了你的其他优点。
You would have been less amiable in my eyes had there not been this little unwillingness; but allow me to assure you that I have your respected mother’s permission for this address.
如果没有这小小的害羞，我对你来说会显得更不友好，但请相信，我得到了你尊敬的母亲的许可，可以向你提出这方面的求婚。
You can hardly doubt the purport of my discourse, however your natural delicacy may lead you to dissemble; my attentions have been too marked to be mistaken.
你的求婚，我几乎可以肯定，尽管你的自然的轻浮会阻止你，但我的求婚已经足够明显。
Almost as soon as I entered the house I singled you out as the companion of my future life.
我刚一进屋，我就把你选为我未来生活的伴侣。

But before I am run away with by my feelings on this subject, perhaps it will be advisable for me to state my reasons for marrying—and, moreover, for coming into Hertfordshire with the design of selecting a wife, as I certainly did.”
但是，我还没有被我的感情带走，也许我应该先陈述一下我结婚的原因——而且，我也有一个计划，打算到赫特福德郡来挑选一个妻子，因为我确实有这个打算。

The idea of Mr. Collins, with all his solemn composure, being run away with by his feelings, made Elizabeth so near laughing that she could not use the short pause he allowed in any attempt to stop him farther, and he continued,—
也许查尔斯先生，尽管他严肃得像一个圣人，也会被他的感情带走，这使丽兹几乎要笑出声来，她不能用她允许的短暂停顿来阻止他，他继续说：

“My reasons for marrying are, first, that I think it a right thing for every clergyman in easy circumstances (like myself) to set the example of matrimony in his parish; secondly, that I am convinced it will add very greatly to my happiness; and, thirdly, which perhaps I ought to have mentioned earlier, that it is the particular advice and recommendation of the very noble lady whom I have the honour of calling patroness.
“结婚的理由，首先，我认为，对于经济上便利的牧师来说，树立婚姻的榜样是理所当然的；其次，我相信这将大大增加我的幸福；第三，也许我应该早些提到，那就是我尊敬的那位贵妇人的特别建议。

Twice has she condescended to give me her opinion (unasked too!) on this subject; and it was but the very Saturday night before I left Hunsford,—between our pools at quadrille, while Mrs. Jenkinson was arranging Miss De Bourgh’s footstool,—that she said, ‘Mr.
她两次向我表示过意见（甚至没有请求过），而且是在我离开亨斯福德之前，就在我们踢球的时候，我太太正在安排德伯格小姐的脚凳——那天晚上，她对我说：“查尔斯先生，你必须结婚。”
Collins, you must marry.
查尔斯先生。
A clergyman like you must marry.
像你这样的神职人员必须结婚。
Choose properly, choose a gentlewoman for my sake, and for your own; let her be an active, useful sort of person, not brought up high, but able to make a small income go a good way.
选择得当，选择一位淑女为我的缘故，也为了你的缘故；让她成为一位勤劳有用的人，而不是出身高贵，但能赚取小钱也能花得好的。
This is my advice.
这是我的建议。
Find such a woman as soon as you can, bring her to Hunsford, and I will visit her.’
找到这样一位女子，带到亨斯福德，我会拜访她的。
Allow me, by the way, to observe, my fair cousin, that I do not reckon the notice and kindness of Lady Catherine de Bourgh as among the least of the advantages in my power to offer.
顺便说一下，我的表妹，我并不认为凯瑟琳德布尔沃小姐的注意和友好是我在能力范围内所能提供的最小的有利条件之一。

You will find her manners beyond anything I can describe; and your wit and vivacity, I think, must be acceptable to her, especially when tempered with the silence and respect which her rank will inevitably excite.
你会发现她的举止超过我所能描述的；并且你的机智和活力，我认为，必须与她气质相配，尤其是当她的地位激发的沉默和尊敬与她身份相配时。

Thus much for my general intention in favour of matrimony; it remains to be told why my views were directed to Longbourn instead of my own neighbourhood, where I assure you there are many amiable young women.
至于我对于婚姻的一般意图，我已经说过，它只适用于长伯恩，而不是我自己的地区，我保证你，那里有许多可爱的年轻女子。

But the fact is, that being, as I am, to inherit this estate after the death of your honoured father (who, however, may live many years longer), I could not satisfy myself without resolving to choose a wife from among his daughters, that the loss to them might be as little as possible when the melancholy event takes place—which, however, as I have already said, may not be for several years.
但事实是，因为我是一个继承者，我死后长伯恩的遗产（虽然我父亲可能活很多年），我不能满足自己，除非我决定从长伯恩的女儿中选择一个妻子，这样，当这个悲哀的事件发生时，她们的损失最小——然而，正如我之前所说，这可能不会几年。
This has been my motive, my fair cousin, and I flatter myself it will not sink me in your esteem.
这是我的动机，我的表妹，我相信这不会降低你对我的情感。
And now nothing remains for me but to assure you in the most animated language of the violence of my affection.
现在我只剩下向你表达我爱情的最强烈的情感。

To fortune I am perfectly indifferent, and shall make no demand of that nature on your father, since I am well aware that it could not be complied with; and that one thousand pounds in the 4 per cents., which will not be yours till after your mother’s decease, is all that you may ever be entitled to.
对于我来说，一切都无关紧要，我不会向你父亲提出这种要求，因为我很清楚，这不可能实现；而且，我1000英镑的利息，直到你母亲去世后，你永远不会得到。
On that head, therefore, I shall be uniformly silent: and you may assure yourself that no ungenerous reproach shall ever pass my lips when we are married.”
在这一点上，我将保持沉默：你可以保证自己，我们结婚后，没有任何不仁的指责会从我口中说出。
It was absolutely necessary to interrupt him now.
现在必须打断他。
“You are too hasty, sir,” she cried.
“你太急了，先生，”她喊道。
“You forget that I have made no answer.
“你忘记了，我没有回答。
Let me do it without further loss of time.
让我尽快完成。
